programme.title: Dashcam Justice
programme.desc: A recovery truck ploughs into an SUV carrying a mother and daughter, sending it flying into another car. The driver insists he's done nothing wrong, but a bus dashcam holds crucial evidence. A minor moped collision sparks a claim for tens of thousands of pounds, and a fraud investigator uncovers suspicious connections. Could the claimant's own footage expose the scam? An HGV leaves a cyclist perilously short of room.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Martin, Dion and Martel check out auction property buys in Plymouth, Silsden in West Yorkshire and the village of Mytholmroyd near Hebden Bridge. The developers do a lot of the work themselves in the hope they can make a profit on their bricks-and-mortar investments.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: The teams are shopping in the mid-Wales town of Builth Wells, and Danny learns about a unique family business which immortalises rugby players and other Welsh icons in clay.

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: Denise van Outen is stepping into the fight against fraud - and this time, it’s personal. After scammers stole thousands from her in a devious bank scam two years ago, Denise is teaming up with Scam Interceptors to turn the tables. In this special episode, airing as part of BBC Scam Safe week, Denise joins Rav Wilding and the team to expose the global web of criminals targeting UK victims, including those taking advantage of her identity. Using the same remote access tech scammers rely on, the team hacks the hackers to monitor their operations in real time, before confronting them. Denise also uses voice-changing technology to have fun at the scammers’ expense.

programme.title: Doorbell Detectives
programme.desc: When one of Nottingham’s oldest businesses is broken into, staff member Becca turns Miss Marple and manages to crack the case. Former police inspector Anton Sullivan shows two residents of the doorbell detective neighbourhood the elaborate lengths thieves will go to, to get their hands on your stuff. And Matt also hears from two friends whose life savings disappeared overnight when their food truck was stolen.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Nicki Chapman is in glorious Gloucestershire with Sam and Mandy, who are moving from a harbour town in Devon and making a fresh start in the countryside, with their two much-loved dogs coming along for the adventure. With £475,000 to spend, Nicki serves up a terrific selection of homes, but it’s the mystery house that really raises the stakes, with views so spectacular they feel like they’re standing on top of the world. From one grand outlook to another, Nicki gets an exclusive invitation to experience horticulture on a truly regal scale when she visits a garden quite literally fit for a king.

programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road
programme.desc: The team help commemorate the victims of the Lockerbie bombing, automata expert Michael tackles a clockwork train, and Kirsten gets hands-on with medieval slipware pottery.

programme.title: The Finish Line
programme.desc: Roman Kemp, assisted by Sarah Greene, hosts the quiz show where contestants race in moving podiums across the studio floor. Correct answers get the players moving, while wrong answers will stop them in their tracks. Five contestants - Amanda, Jamie, Iain, Namita and Chris - battle across a series of fast-paced qualifiers and head-to-head races where the aim of the game is simple – make it to the finish line before your rivals. The winner then races against the track itself in an attempt to win the £5,000 cash prize.

programme.title: Pointless
programme.desc: Alexander Armstrong is joined by co-host Vick Hope for the brainy quiz where the contestants try to score as few points as possible by plumbing the depths of their general knowledge to come up with the answers no-one else could think of.

programme.title: The Marvellous Miniature Workshop
programme.desc: Sara Cox and the team meet Steven, a fourth-generation baker who longs to see his family’s beloved bakery brought back to life in miniature. Once the heart of local life, the business has since been lost to changing times. Can Lee Robinson capture the shopfront, the loaves and the legacy that meant everything to Steven’s family?

programme.title: The Witch Farm
programme.desc: The family receive a shockingly high electricity bill, and their animals start to behave oddly. Liz meets spiritualist Bethan at a mother and baby group. After a strained Christmas dinner, Jonathan admits he’s also seen a ghost. Liz and Bill beg Brecon Council for help, raising the suspicions of social services. Bethan offers to conduct a seance, leading to a shocking conclusion.

programme.title: Have I Got News for You
programme.desc: Kelly Cates hosts, with guest panellists comedian Maisie Adam and journalist Krishnan Guru-Murthy joining team captains Ian Hislop and Paul Merton as they delve into the news.

programme.title: The Traitors Ireland
programme.desc: The doors of Slane Castle have opened once again, with 23 new players entering The Traitors Ireland for its second season. The line-up features contestants from across the country, ranging in age from 24 to 61 and including teachers, a postal worker, a psychotherapist, a musician, a stay-at-home dad, an Irish Defence Forces member, and an actor and drama teacher. Hosted once again by Siobhán McSweeney, the players attempt to navigate a game built on trust, strategy and deception, forming alliances while trying to work out who among them they can believe.

programme.title: Saturday Kitchen
programme.desc: Matt Tebbutt is joined by chefs Saliha Mahmood-Ahmed and The Beefy Boys, and by special guest Greg Wise. Drinks expert Helen McGinn picks the wines to go with the studio dishes, and there are some great moments from the BBC food archive.

programme.title: Simply Nigella
programme.desc: There is another serving of irresistibly easy dishes on offer as Nigella rustles up more of her favourite recipes that promise to help with the wind down at the end of a long day. This time, the focus is on ensuring a cosy and comforting vibe. Breakfast is a tray of cheering chai muffins - light, luscious and dairy-free. For a low-key lunch, there are Nigella's Asian-flavoured short ribs - a perfect make-ahead, meltingly tender beef stew. And friends are in for an informal supper with Nigella's fish tacos. Inspired by her visits to Tacoria's on America's west coast, Nigella's homemade, oven-baked version involves a bit of DIY at the table, ensuring a laid-back atmosphere for guests and host alike. The tacos are followed by a divine salted chocolate tart for pudding.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: This special show is just what the doctor ordered! Experts Gary Pe and Steph Connell help actors Dex Lee, Kia Pegg, Sarah Moyle and Dido Miles in their hunt for healthy profits.

programme.title: The Football Interview
programme.desc: The Football Interview sees the biggest names in sport and entertainment join host Kelly Somers for bold, in-depth conversations about the nation’s favourite sport. We explore mindset and motivation, reflect on defining moments and career highs, and discuss personal insights. It’s a chance to show an honest, human and sometimes surprising side to familiar faces. At the heart of this is Kelly Somers – one of the most trusted, versatile and authentic voices in sports broadcasting. Kelly brings a brand of warmth and relatability that resonates with both athletes and audiences. What sets her apart is her ability to dig deeper with a sensitive approach, creating a space where athletes feel comfortable being open, honest and at times vulnerable. Each episode sees Kelly draw out stories and insight from the player behind the name about the beautiful game, their origins and values, and a look-ahead to the future from a sporting and personal perspective. She takes her subjects on a journey – and takes the viewer with her.

programme.title: BBC Weekend News
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: In Surrey, Sarah Moore is at Witley recycling centre, trawling the car boots in the hope of finding some potential gems in need of creative magic. Upcycling sisters Katie Stone and Sophie Lawrence are tested by a wooden cabinet in disrepair, four chairs in a mix of styles get a radical revamp from woodworker Martin Hough, whilst Sarah must think out of the box when she takes on a metal trunk full of vintage tools.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Martin is overcome by the mould at a Southampton semi. Owain loves the 70s period charm on offer in Herefordshire. And Jacqui is in upmarket Chelsea, but the flat she’s in is not as fashionable as the area... at least for now!

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: A creative couple from London want to leave city life behind in search of new adventures in Gloucestershire, and Chris Bavin is on hand to guide them. Along with presenting a lovely selection of houses, Chris also visits a local football club to check out for himself why it’s green by name and green by nature.

programme.title: Final Score
programme.desc: Jason Mohammad and guests bring you all the goals, latest drama, analysis, reaction and interviews.

programme.title: BBC Weekend News
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Spotlight
programme.desc: The latest news, sport, weather and features from the South West of England.

programme.title: The Famous Finish Line
programme.desc: Roman Kemp hosts this quiz show with sidekick Sarah Greene. Five celebrities, Maisie Adam, JJ Chalmers, Harry Clark, Abby Cook and Colin Jackson, race in moving podiums across a star-spangled themed studio to try to win £10,000 for their chosen charity.

programme.title: Strictly Come Dancing
programme.desc: It’s that time of year again – Strictly returns to the home of ballroom dancing, the iconic Blackpool Tower, for a spectacular night of dancing. The show begins with a group performance from the entire cast and the legendary Basement Jaxx. Then, Emma, Josh and Jojo welcome our couples to the world-famous ballroom for their biggest performances of the competition. Shirley Ballas, Craig Revel Horwood, Motsi Mabuse and Anton Du Beke have packed their paddles and will be sharing expert advice before the vote opens and you have your say. Which couple’s performance will be the talk of the tower?

programme.title: Michael McIntyre's The Wheel
programme.desc: Michael McIntyre hosts his hit game show packed with huge stars, big laughs and a giant spinning wheel. Can the contestants answer their way to a fortune? The celebrity experts in this episode are Italian Bach, Kerry Godliman, Trevor Nelson, Angela Scanlon, Alex Scott, Josh Widdicombe, Bez and Shaun Ryder.

programme.title: Honey
programme.desc: Martha is annoyed after Kurt steals their joint credit for locating Kamilla, and she vows to gain access to the scientist alone. A competitive Kurt promises to do the same. Friedrich is ordered by his boss Schimmel to ramp up his efforts to locate Greta, believing she is the key to the Hermann Metzl case. Eager for a win, Martha and Kurt attempt to insinuate their way into Friedrich’s confidence to find Greta. Stung by his reaction, Martha steals a prized possession.

programme.title: BBC Weekend News
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Match of the Day
programme.desc: Highlights of seven Premier League games, including leaders Arsenal, who travel to Newcastle. Manchester City have a home game against Fulham as they look to end a three-match losing run. Bottom-of-the-table Crystal Palace travel to Coventry, whilst Chelsea welcome Leeds to Stamford Bridge. Elsewhere, in-form Bournemouth host Nottingham Forest, Aston Villa take on Sunderland, and Ipswich make the trip to Spurs. Presented by Gabby Logan, with Joe Hart and Alan Shearer.

programme.title: Far from the Madding Crowd
programme.desc: Beautiful and headstrong Bathsheba Everdene catches the eye of local farmer Gabriel Oak when she arrives to live with her aunt in the Dorset village of Norcombe. She declines his offer of marriage, but their lives continue to intertwine as fate brings contrasting fortunes to both of them. Adapted by David Nicholls for BBC Films from the novel by Thomas Hardy.

programme.title: Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg
programme.desc: The big names behind the big stories. Laura Kuenssberg talks to those making the news, inside and outside politics.

programme.title: Politics South West
programme.desc: Martyn Oates with the latest political news and debate.

programme.title: Sunday Morning Live
programme.desc: Sean Fletcher and Holly Hamilton host a pre-recorded, end-of-year episode of the show that puts the heart and soul into Sundays, bringing faith and ethics to the discussions that matter most. We reflect on a year when warnings of the risks facing humanity have regularly been in the news and examine the impact these themes could have on society as we ask: can a crisis bring us together? And, a year after Dame Sarah Mullally was formally elected as archbishop of Canterbury, we discuss what the future of the church could look like. We also hear the story of the Scottish teenager who could become a saint.

programme.title: Celebration Kitchen
programme.desc: Matt Tebbutt is joined by chefs Gurdeep Loyal, Ravinder Bhogal and Manpreet Singh. Celebrity guests Ranvir Singh, Dr Ranj and Sathnam Sanghera celebrate the Sikh festival Guru Nanak Gurpurab.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: From the Golden Globes to the Emmys, it’s awards season on the show as Natasha Raskin Sharp marvels at movie memorabilia, all owned by a familiar face – Bargain Hunt expert and film fan Stephanie Connell. Steph shares with Natasha items from her own collection, including awards given to Sir John Gielgud and an original prop from 1970 film Julius Caesar, starring Charlton Heston. In a Brackley antiques centre, two teams hope to find some blockbuster buys of their own, helped by leading men Tim Weeks and Thomas Forrester. And in the grand finale at the auction in Derbyshire, auctioneer James Lewis gives his verdict on the teams’ items.

programme.title: Simply Nigella
programme.desc: There is another serving of irresistibly easy dishes on offer as Nigella rustles up more of her favourite recipes that promise to help with the wind down at the end of a long day. This time, the focus is on ensuring a cosy and comforting vibe. Breakfast is a tray of cheering chai muffins - light, luscious and dairy-free. For a low-key lunch, there are Nigella's Asian-flavoured short ribs - a perfect make-ahead, meltingly tender beef stew. And friends are in for an informal supper with Nigella's fish tacos. programme.title: The Football Interview
programme.desc: The Football Interview sees the biggest names in sport and entertainment join host Kelly Somers for bold, in-depth conversations about the nation’s favourite sport. We explore mindset and motivation, reflect on defining moments and career highs, and discuss personal insights. It’s a chance to show an honest, human and sometimes surprising side to familiar faces. At the heart of this is Kelly Somers – one of the most trusted, versatile and authentic voices in sports broadcasting. Kelly brings a brand of warmth and relatability that resonates with both athletes and audiences. What sets her apart is her ability to dig deeper with a sensitive approach, creating a space where athletes feel comfortable being open, honest and at times vulnerable. Each episode sees Kelly draw out stories and insight from the player behind the name about the beautiful game, their origins and values, and a look-ahead to the future from a sporting and personal perspective. She takes her subjects on a journey – and takes the viewer with her.

In a Brackley antiques centre, two teams hope to find some blockbuster buys of their own, helped by leading men Tim Weeks and Thomas Forrester. And in the grand finale at the auction in Derbyshire, auctioneer James Lewis gives his verdict on the teams’ items.

Charlotte finds out why Claire made the leap into farming and what regenerative farming means to her, before helping with health and pregnancy checks on her cattle. Sean gets stuck into a cow pat to explore the hidden world of dung beetles and helps plant trees in a new agroforestry field. Meanwhile, Tom investigates changes that could be coming for the game bird shooting industry.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: The roadshow comes from Alexandra Gardens in the heart of Cardiff, where treasures include a Maori pipe, a book listing wartime spies and a rare SAS medal collection. Ronnie Archer-Morgan is thrilled to see a pipe by a renowned Maori craftsman, whilst Geoffrey Munn is dazzled by a jewel-encrusted stick pin given as a gift from King Edward VII and Queen Alexandra. There are plenty of Welsh treasures to be found, including an autograph book featuring a Tom Jones signature and early concert ticket, and Lisa Lloyd challenges Fiona to spot the most valuable item in a group of three pieces of rare rugby memorabilia. Marc Allum is stunned to see a remarkable archive of First World War-era photographs documenting arrivals into Cardiff Docks, some of whom were suspected of being spies, and militaria expert Mark Smith is humbled by a group of medals and a cap badge belonging to one of the earliest members of the SAS. Fiona Bruce finds out about the long history of Alexandra Gardens as a war memorial when she meets Simon Weston, veteran of the Falklands conflict.

programme.title: Strictly Come Dancing

Manchester City have a home game against Fulham as they look to end a three-match losing run. Bottom-of-the-table Crystal Palace travel to Coventry, whilst Chelsea welcome Leeds to Stamford Bridge. Elsewhere, in-form Bournemouth host Nottingham Forest, Aston Villa take on Sunderland, and Ipswich make the trip to Spurs. Presented by Gabby Logan, with Joe Hart and Alan Shearer.

programme.title: Far from the Madding Crowd
programme.desc: Beautiful and headstrong Bathsheba Everdene catches the eye of local farmer Gabriel Oak when she arrives to live with her aunt in the Dorset village of Norcombe. She declines his offer of marriage, but their lives continue to intertwine as fate brings contrasting fortunes to both of them. Adapted by David Nicholls for BBC Films from the novel by Thomas Hardy.

programme.title: Politics East Midlands
programme.desc: Peter Saull with political news, interviews and debate.

programme.title: Sunday Morning Live
programme.desc: Sean Fletcher and Holly Hamilton host a pre-recorded, end-of-year episode of the show that puts the heart and soul into Sundays, bringing faith and ethics to the discussions that matter most. We reflect on a year when warnings of the risks facing humanity have regularly been in the news and examine the impact these themes could have on society as we ask: can a crisis bring us together? And, a year after Dame Sarah Mullally was formally elected as archbishop of Canterbury, we discuss what the future of the church could look like. We also hear the story of the Scottish teenager who could become a saint.

programme.title: Celebration Kitchen
programme.desc: Matt Tebbutt is joined by chefs Gurdeep Loyal, Ravinder Bhogal and Manpreet Singh. Celebrity guests Ranvir Singh, Dr Ranj and Sathnam Sanghera celebrate the Sikh festival Guru Nanak Gurpurab.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: From the Golden Globes to the Emmys, it’s awards season on the show as Natasha Raskin Sharp marvels at movie memorabilia, all owned by a familiar face – Bargain Hunt expert and film fan Stephanie Connell. Steph shares with Natasha items from her own collection, including awards given to Sir John Gielgud and an original prop from 1970 film Julius Caesar, starring Charlton Heston. In a Brackley antiques centre, two teams hope to find some blockbuster buys of their own, helped by leading men Tim Weeks and Thomas Forrester. And in the grand finale at the auction in Derbyshire, auctioneer James Lewis gives his verdict on the teams’ items.

programme.title: Nativity 2: Danger in the Manger!
programme.desc: An anxious teacher starts a new job at an under-achieving school and quickly finds himself struggling to cope with a wild classroom assistant, a group of under-performing kids and his own very pregnant wife. He soon becomes embroiled in a madcap plan to enter a national Song for Christmas competition and finds himself embarking on a disastrous road trip in search of the competition venue - the Christmas Castle. programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Charlotte Smith and Sean Fletcher are in the Ceiriog Valley in north Wales, meeting former clinical vet Claire Whittle, who took on an upland farm two years ago. Charlotte finds out why Claire made the leap into farming and what regenerative farming means to her, before helping with health and pregnancy checks on her cattle. Sean gets stuck into a cow pat to explore the hidden world of dung beetles and helps plant trees in a new agroforestry field. Meanwhile, Tom investigates changes that could be coming for the game bird shooting industry.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: The roadshow comes from Alexandra Gardens in the heart of Cardiff, where treasures include a Maori pipe, a book listing wartime spies and a rare SAS medal collection. Ronnie Archer-Morgan is thrilled to see a pipe by a renowned Maori craftsman, whilst Geoffrey Munn is dazzled by a jewel-encrusted stick pin given as a gift from King Edward VII and Queen Alexandra. There are plenty of Welsh treasures to be found, including an autograph book featuring a Tom Jones signature and early concert ticket, and Lisa Lloyd challenges Fiona to spot the most valuable item in a group of three pieces of rare rugby memorabilia. Marc Allum is stunned to see a remarkable archive of First World War-era photographs documenting arrivals into Cardiff Docks, some of whom were suspected of being spies, and militaria expert Mark Smith is humbled by a group of medals and a cap badge belonging to one of the earliest members of the SAS. Fiona Bruce finds out about the long history of Alexandra Gardens as a war memorial when she meets Simon Weston, veteran of the Falklands conflict.

programme.title: Strictly Come Dancing
programme.desc: It’s part two of the Blackpool spectacular, and we’re back in the Tower Ballroom for the results. The pros hit the dance floor for another dazzling group performance before two couples must dance again to try to keep their place in the competition. Who will dance for the final time in Blackpool? And who will return for an Instant Dance next weekend?

programme.title: Blue Planet III
programme.desc: A look at the surprising connections between the world's oceans, from the icy worlds of the poles to unexpected coasts closer to home.

programme.title: The Witch Farm
programme.desc: Summer 1989. Looking for a fresh start, Bill and his pregnant partner Liz move to a remote farmhouse in the idyllic Brecon Beacons with his teenage son Jonathan. Yet on the very first night, Liz hears footsteps on the landing. Before long, she and Jonathan are sharing disturbing dreams. And as strange events intensify, Bill and Liz are forced to accept a terrifying new reality.

programme.title: Dashcam Justice
programme.desc: A recovery truck ploughs into an SUV carrying a mother and daughter, sending it flying into another car. The driver insists he's done nothing wrong, but a bus dashcam holds crucial evidence. A minor moped collision sparks a claim for tens of thousands of pounds, and a fraud investigator uncovers suspicious connections. Could the claimant's own footage expose the scam? An HGV leaves a cyclist perilously short of room.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Martin, Dion and Martel check out auction property buys in Plymouth, Silsden in West Yorkshire and the village of Mytholmroyd near Hebden Bridge. The developers do a lot of the work themselves in the hope they can make a profit on their bricks-and-mortar investments.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: The teams are shopping in the mid-Wales town of Builth Wells, and Danny learns about a unique family business which immortalises rugby players and other Welsh icons in clay.

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: Denise van Outen is stepping into the fight against fraud - and this time, it’s personal. After scammers stole thousands from her in a devious bank scam two years ago, Denise is teaming up with Scam Interceptors to turn the tables. In this special episode, airing as part of BBC Scam Safe week, Denise joins Rav Wilding and the team to expose the global web of criminals targeting UK victims, including those taking advantage of her identity. Using the same remote access tech scammers rely on, the team hacks the hackers to monitor their operations in real time, before confronting them. Denise also uses voice-changing technology to have fun at the scammers’ expense.

programme.title: Doorbell Detectives
programme.desc: When one of Nottingham’s oldest businesses is broken into, staff member Becca turns Miss Marple and manages to crack the case. Former police inspector Anton Sullivan shows two residents of the doorbell detective neighbourhood the elaborate lengths thieves will go to, to get their hands on your stuff. And Matt also hears from two friends whose life savings disappeared overnight when their food truck was stolen.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Nicki Chapman is in glorious Gloucestershire with Sam and Mandy, who are moving from a harbour town in Devon and making a fresh start in the countryside, with their two much-loved dogs coming along for the adventure. With £475,000 to spend, Nicki serves up a terrific selection of homes, but it’s the mystery house that really raises the stakes, with views so spectacular they feel like they’re standing on top of the world. From one grand outlook to another, Nicki gets an exclusive invitation to experience horticulture on a truly regal scale when she visits a garden quite literally fit for a king.

programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road
programme.desc: The team help commemorate the victims of the Lockerbie bombing, automata expert Michael tackles a clockwork train, and Kirsten gets hands-on with medieval slipware pottery.

programme.title: The Finish Line
programme.desc: Roman Kemp, assisted by Sarah Greene, hosts the quiz show where contestants race in moving podiums across the studio floor. Correct answers get the players moving, while wrong answers will stop them in their tracks. Five contestants - Amanda, Jamie, Iain, Namita and Chris - battle across a series of fast-paced qualifiers and head-to-head races where the aim of the game is simple – make it to the finish line before your rivals. The winner then races against the track itself in an attempt to win the £5,000 cash prize.

programme.title: Pointless
programme.desc: Alexander Armstrong is joined by co-host Vick Hope for the brainy quiz where the contestants try to score as few points as possible by plumbing the depths of their general knowledge to come up with the answers no-one else could think of.

programme.title: EastEnders
programme.desc: Eve finds herself grappling with the aftermath. Gina's search for answers takes an unexpected turn. Family tensions continue to simmer for the Carters.

programme.title: The Marvellous Miniature Workshop
programme.desc: Sara Cox and the team meet Steven, a fourth-generation baker who longs to see his family’s beloved bakery brought back to life in miniature. Once the heart of local life, the business has since been lost to changing times. Can Lee Robinson capture the shopfront, the loaves and the legacy that meant everything to Steven’s family?

programme.title: The Witch Farm
programme.desc: The family receive a shockingly high electricity bill, and their animals start to behave oddly. Liz meets spiritualist Bethan at a mother and baby group. After a strained Christmas dinner, Jonathan admits he’s also seen a ghost. Liz and Bill beg Brecon Council for help, raising the suspicions of social services. Bethan offers to conduct a seance, leading to a shocking conclusion.

programme.desc: The latest national and international news, with reports from BBC correspondents worldwide.

programme.title: Have I Got News for You
programme.desc: Kelly Cates hosts, with guest panellists comedian Maisie Adam and journalist Krishnan Guru-Murthy joining team captains Ian Hislop and Paul Merton as they delve into the news.

programme.title: The Traitors Ireland
programme.desc: The doors of Slane Castle have opened once again, with 23 new players entering The Traitors Ireland for its second season. The line-up features contestants from across the country, ranging in age from 24 to 61 and including teachers, a postal worker, a psychotherapist, a musician, a stay-at-home dad, an Irish Defence Forces member, and an actor and drama teacher. Hosted once again by Siobhán McSweeney, the players attempt to navigate a game built on trust, strategy and deception, forming alliances while trying to work out who among them they can believe.

programme.title: Saturday Kitchen
programme.desc: Matt Tebbutt is joined by chefs Saliha Mahmood-Ahmed and The Beefy Boys, and by special guest Greg Wise. Drinks expert Helen McGinn picks the wines to go with the studio dishes, and there are some great moments from the BBC food archive.

programme.title: Simply Nigella
programme.desc: There is another serving of irresistibly easy dishes on offer as Nigella rustles up more of her favourite recipes that promise to help with the wind down at the end of a long day. This time, the focus is on ensuring a cosy and comforting vibe. Breakfast is a tray of cheering chai muffins - light, luscious and dairy-free. For a low-key lunch, there are Nigella's Asian-flavoured short ribs - a perfect make-ahead, meltingly tender beef stew. And friends are in for an informal supper with Nigella's fish tacos. Inspired by her visits to Tacoria's on America's west coast, Nigella's homemade, oven-baked version involves a bit of DIY at the table, ensuring a laid-back atmosphere for guests and host alike. The tacos are followed by a divine salted chocolate tart for pudding.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: This special show is just what the doctor ordered! Experts Gary Pe and Steph Connell help actors Dex Lee, Kia Pegg, Sarah Moyle and Dido Miles in their hunt for healthy profits.

programme.title: The Football Interview
programme.desc: The Football Interview sees the biggest names in sport and entertainment join host Kelly Somers for bold, in-depth conversations about the nation’s favourite sport. We explore mindset and motivation, reflect on defining moments and career highs, and discuss personal insights. It’s a chance to show an honest, human and sometimes surprising side to familiar faces. At the heart of this is Kelly Somers – one of the most trusted, versatile and authentic voices in sports broadcasting. Kelly brings a brand of warmth and relatability that resonates with both athletes and audiences. What sets her apart is her ability to dig deeper with a sensitive approach, creating a space where athletes feel comfortable being open, honest and at times vulnerable. Each episode sees Kelly draw out stories and insight from the player behind the name about the beautiful game, their origins and values, and a look-ahead to the future from a sporting and personal perspective. She takes her subjects on a journey – and takes the viewer with her.

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: In Surrey, Sarah Moore is at Witley recycling centre, trawling the car boots in the hope of finding some potential gems in need of creative magic. Upcycling sisters Katie Stone and Sophie Lawrence are tested by a wooden cabinet in disrepair, four chairs in a mix of styles get a radical revamp from woodworker Martin Hough, whilst Sarah must think out of the box when she takes on a metal trunk full of vintage tools.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Martin is overcome by the mould at a Southampton semi. Owain loves the 70s period charm on offer in Herefordshire. And Jacqui is in upmarket Chelsea, but the flat she’s in is not as fashionable as the area... at least for now!

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: A creative couple from London want to leave city life behind in search of new adventures in Gloucestershire, and Chris Bavin is on hand to guide them. Along with presenting a lovely selection of houses, Chris also visits a local football club to check out for himself why it’s green by name and green by nature.

programme.title: Final Score
programme.desc: Jason Mohammad and guests bring you all the goals, latest drama, analysis, reaction and interviews.

programme.title: Look North (Yorkshire)
programme.desc: The latest news, sport and weather for Yorkshire.

programme.title: The Famous Finish Line
programme.desc: Roman Kemp hosts this quiz show with sidekick Sarah Greene. Five celebrities, Maisie Adam, JJ Chalmers, Harry Clark, Abby Cook and Colin Jackson, race in moving podiums across a star-spangled themed studio to try to win £10,000 for their chosen charity.

programme.title: Strictly Come Dancing
programme.desc: It’s that time of year again – Strictly returns to the home of ballroom dancing, the iconic Blackpool Tower, for a spectacular night of dancing. The show begins with a group performance from the entire cast and the legendary Basement Jaxx. Then, Emma, Josh and Jojo welcome our couples to the world-famous ballroom for their biggest performances of the competition. Shirley Ballas, Craig Revel Horwood, Motsi Mabuse and Anton Du Beke have packed their paddles and will be sharing expert advice before the vote opens and you have your say. Which couple’s performance will be the talk of the tower?

programme.title: Michael McIntyre's The Wheel
programme.desc: Michael McIntyre hosts his hit game show packed with huge stars, big laughs and a giant spinning wheel. Can the contestants answer their way to a fortune? The celebrity experts in this episode are Italian Bach, Kerry Godliman, Trevor Nelson, Angela Scanlon, Alex Scott, Josh Widdicombe, Bez and Shaun Ryder.

programme.title: Honey
programme.desc: Martha is annoyed after Kurt steals their joint credit for locating Kamilla, and she vows to gain access to the scientist alone. A competitive Kurt promises to do the same. Friedrich is ordered by his boss Schimmel to ramp up his efforts to locate Greta, believing she is the key to the Hermann Metzl case. Eager for a win, Martha and Kurt attempt to insinuate their way into Friedrich’s confidence to find Greta. Stung by his reaction, Martha steals a prized possession.

The driver insists he's done nothing wrong, but a bus dashcam holds crucial evidence. A minor moped collision sparks a claim for tens of thousands of pounds, and a fraud investigator uncovers suspicious connections. Could the claimant's own footage expose the scam? An HGV leaves a cyclist perilously short of room.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Martin, Dion and Martel check out auction property buys in Plymouth, Silsden in West Yorkshire and the village of Mytholmroyd near Hebden Bridge. The developers do a lot of the work themselves in the hope they can make a profit on their bricks-and-mortar investments.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: The teams are shopping in the mid-Wales town of Builth Wells, and Danny learns about a unique family business which immortalises rugby players and other Welsh icons in clay.

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: Denise van Outen is stepping into the fight against fraud - and this time, it’s personal. After scammers stole thousands from her in a devious bank scam two years ago, Denise is teaming up with Scam Interceptors to turn the tables. In this special episode, airing as part of BBC Scam Safe week, Denise joins Rav Wilding and the team to expose the global web of criminals targeting UK victims, including those taking advantage of her identity. Using the same remote access tech scammers rely on, the team hacks the hackers to monitor their operations in real time, before confronting them. Denise also uses voice-changing technology to have fun at the scammers’ expense.

programme.title: Doorbell Detectives
programme.desc: When one of Nottingham’s oldest businesses is broken into, staff member Becca turns Miss Marple and manages to crack the case. Former police inspector Anton Sullivan shows two residents of the doorbell detective neighbourhood the elaborate lengths thieves will go to, to get their hands on your stuff. And Matt also hears from two friends whose life savings disappeared overnight when their food truck was stolen.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Nicki Chapman is in glorious Gloucestershire with Sam and Mandy, who are moving from a harbour town in Devon and making a fresh start in the countryside, with their two much-loved dogs coming along for the adventure. With £475,000 to spend, Nicki serves up a terrific selection of homes, but it’s the mystery house that really raises the stakes, with views so spectacular they feel like they’re standing on top of the world. From one grand outlook to another, Nicki gets an exclusive invitation to experience horticulture on a truly regal scale when she visits a garden quite literally fit for a king.

programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road
programme.desc: The team help commemorate the victims of the Lockerbie bombing, automata expert Michael tackles a clockwork train, and Kirsten gets hands-on with medieval slipware pottery.

programme.title: The Finish Line
programme.desc: Roman Kemp, assisted by Sarah Greene, hosts the quiz show where contestants race in moving podiums across the studio floor. Correct answers get the players moving, while wrong answers will stop them in their tracks. Five contestants - Amanda, Jamie, Iain, Namita and Chris - battle across a series of fast-paced qualifiers and head-to-head races where the aim of the game is simple – make it to the finish line before your rivals. The winner then races against the track itself in an attempt to win the £5,000 cash prize.

programme.title: Pointless
programme.desc: Alexander Armstrong is joined by co-host Vick Hope for the brainy quiz where the contestants try to score as few points as possible by plumbing the depths of their general knowledge to come up with the answers no-one else could think of.

programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.desc: The latest news, sport and weather for Yorkshire.

programme.title: The One Show

programme.title: EastEnders
programme.desc: Eve finds herself grappling with the aftermath. Gina's search for answers takes an unexpected turn. Family tensions continue to simmer for the Carters.

programme.title: The Witch Farm
programme.desc: The family receive a shockingly high electricity bill, and their animals start to behave oddly. Liz meets spiritualist Bethan at a mother and baby group. After a strained Christmas dinner, Jonathan admits he’s also seen a ghost. Liz and Bill beg Brecon Council for help, raising the suspicions of social services. Bethan offers to conduct a seance, leading to a shocking conclusion.

programme.title: Have I Got News for You
programme.desc: Kelly Cates hosts, with guest panellists comedian Maisie Adam and journalist Krishnan Guru-Murthy joining team captains Ian Hislop and Paul Merton as they delve into the news.

programme.title: The Traitors Ireland
programme.desc: The doors of Slane Castle have opened once again, with 23 new players entering The Traitors Ireland for its second season. The line-up features contestants from across the country, ranging in age from 24 to 61 and including teachers, a postal worker, a psychotherapist, a musician, a stay-at-home dad, an Irish Defence Forces member, and an actor and drama teacher. Hosted once again by Siobhán McSweeney, the players attempt to navigate a game built on trust, strategy and deception, forming alliances while trying to work out who among them they can believe.

programme.title: Breakfast

programme.title: Saturday Kitchen
programme.desc: Matt Tebbutt is joined by chefs Saliha Mahmood-Ahmed and The Beefy Boys, and by special guest Greg Wise. Drinks expert Helen McGinn picks the wines to go with the studio dishes, and there are some great moments from the BBC food archive.

programme.title: Simply Nigella
programme.desc: There is another serving of irresistibly easy dishes on offer as Nigella rustles up more of her favourite recipes that promise to help with the wind down at the end of a long day. This time, the focus is on ensuring a cosy and comforting vibe. Breakfast is a tray of cheering chai muffins - light, luscious and dairy-free. For a low-key lunch, there are Nigella's Asian-flavoured short ribs - a perfect make-ahead, meltingly tender beef stew. And friends are in for an informal supper with Nigella's fish tacos. Inspired by her visits to Tacoria's on America's west coast, Nigella's homemade, oven-baked version involves a bit of DIY at the table, ensuring a laid-back atmosphere for guests and host alike. The tacos are followed by a divine salted chocolate tart for pudding.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: This special show is just what the doctor ordered! Experts Gary Pe and Steph Connell help actors Dex Lee, Kia Pegg, Sarah Moyle and Dido Miles in their hunt for healthy profits.

programme.title: The Football Interview
programme.desc: The Football Interview sees the biggest names in sport and entertainment join host Kelly Somers for bold, in-depth conversations about the nation’s favourite sport. We explore mindset and motivation, reflect on defining moments and career highs, and discuss personal insights. It’s a chance to show an honest, human and sometimes surprising side to familiar faces. At the heart of this is Kelly Somers – one of the most trusted, versatile and authentic voices in sports broadcasting. Kelly brings a brand of warmth and relatability that resonates with both athletes and audiences. What sets her apart is her ability to dig deeper with a sensitive approach, creating a space where athletes feel comfortable being open, honest and at times vulnerable. Each episode sees Kelly draw out stories and insight from the player behind the name about the beautiful game, their origins and values, and a look-ahead to the future from a sporting and personal perspective. She takes her subjects on a journey – and takes the viewer with her.

programme.title: BBC Weekend News
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: In Surrey, Sarah Moore is at Witley recycling centre, trawling the car boots in the hope of finding some potential gems in need of creative magic. Upcycling sisters Katie Stone and Sophie Lawrence are tested by a wooden cabinet in disrepair, four chairs in a mix of styles get a radical revamp from woodworker Martin Hough, whilst Sarah must think out of the box when she takes on a metal trunk full of vintage tools.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Martin is overcome by the mould at a Southampton semi. Owain loves the 70s period charm on offer in Herefordshire. And Jacqui is in upmarket Chelsea, but the flat she’s in is not as fashionable as the area... at least for now!

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: A creative couple from London want to leave city life behind in search of new adventures in Gloucestershire, and Chris Bavin is on hand to guide them. Along with presenting a lovely selection of houses, Chris also visits a local football club to check out for himself why it’s green by name and green by nature.

programme.title: Final Score
programme.desc: Jason Mohammad and guests bring you all the goals, latest drama, analysis, reaction and interviews.

programme.title: BBC Weekend News
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Look North (North East and Cumbria)
programme.desc: The latest news, sport and weather for the North East and Cumbria.

programme.title: The Famous Finish Line
programme.desc: Roman Kemp hosts this quiz show with sidekick Sarah Greene. Five celebrities, Maisie Adam, JJ Chalmers, Harry Clark, Abby Cook and Colin Jackson, race in moving podiums across a star-spangled themed studio to try to win £10,000 for their chosen charity.

programme.title: Strictly Come Dancing
programme.desc: It’s that time of year again – Strictly returns to the home of ballroom dancing, the iconic Blackpool Tower, for a spectacular night of dancing. The show begins with a group performance from the entire cast and the legendary Basement Jaxx. Then, Emma, Josh and Jojo welcome our couples to the world-famous ballroom for their biggest performances of the competition. Shirley Ballas, Craig Revel Horwood, Motsi Mabuse and Anton Du Beke have packed their paddles and will be sharing expert advice before the vote opens and you have your say. Which couple’s performance will be the talk of the tower?

programme.title: Michael McIntyre's The Wheel
programme.desc: Michael McIntyre hosts his hit game show packed with huge stars, big laughs and a giant spinning wheel. Can the contestants answer their way to a fortune? The celebrity experts in this episode are Italian Bach, Kerry Godliman, Trevor Nelson, Angela Scanlon, Alex Scott, Josh Widdicombe, Bez and Shaun Ryder.

programme.title: Honey
programme.desc: Martha is annoyed after Kurt steals their joint credit for locating Kamilla, and she vows to gain access to the scientist alone. A competitive Kurt promises to do the same. Friedrich is ordered by his boss Schimmel to ramp up his efforts to locate Greta, believing she is the key to the Hermann Metzl case. Eager for a win, Martha and Kurt attempt to insinuate their way into Friedrich’s confidence to find Greta. Stung by his reaction, Martha steals a prized possession.

programme.title: BBC Weekend News
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Match of the Day
programme.desc: Highlights of seven Premier League games, including leaders Arsenal, who travel to Newcastle. Manchester City have a home game against Fulham as they look to end a three-match losing run. Bottom-of-the-table Crystal Palace travel to Coventry, whilst Chelsea welcome Leeds to Stamford Bridge. Elsewhere, in-form Bournemouth host Nottingham Forest, Aston Villa take on Sunderland, and Ipswich make the trip to Spurs. Presented by Gabby Logan, with Joe Hart and Alan Shearer.

programme.title: Far from the Madding Crowd
programme.desc: Beautiful and headstrong Bathsheba Everdene catches the eye of local farmer Gabriel Oak when she arrives to live with her aunt in the Dorset village of Norcombe. She declines his offer of marriage, but their lives continue to intertwine as fate brings contrasting fortunes to both of them. Adapted by David Nicholls for BBC Films from the novel by Thomas Hardy.

programme.title: Politics North (North East and Cumbria)
programme.desc: The latest political news, interviews and debate.

programme.title: Sunday Morning Live
programme.desc: Sean Fletcher and Holly Hamilton host a pre-recorded, end-of-year episode of the show that puts the heart and soul into Sundays, bringing faith and ethics to the discussions that matter most. We reflect on a year when warnings of the risks facing humanity have regularly been in the news and examine the impact these themes could have on society as we ask: can a crisis bring us together? And, a year after Dame Sarah Mullally was formally elected as archbishop of Canterbury, we discuss what the future of the church could look like. We also hear the story of the Scottish teenager who could become a saint.

programme.title: Celebration Kitchen
programme.desc: Matt Tebbutt is joined by chefs Gurdeep Loyal, Ravinder Bhogal and Manpreet Singh. Celebrity guests Ranvir Singh, Dr Ranj and Sathnam Sanghera celebrate the Sikh festival Guru Nanak Gurpurab.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: From the Golden Globes to the Emmys, it’s awards season on the show as Natasha Raskin Sharp marvels at movie memorabilia, all owned by a familiar face – Bargain Hunt expert and film fan Stephanie Connell. Steph shares with Natasha items from her own collection, including awards given to Sir John Gielgud and an original prop from 1970 film Julius Caesar, starring Charlton Heston. In a Brackley antiques centre, two teams hope to find some blockbuster buys of their own, helped by leading men Tim Weeks and Thomas Forrester. And in the grand finale at the auction in Derbyshire, auctioneer James Lewis gives his verdict on the teams’ items.

programme.title: Points of View

programme.title: Songs of Praise
programme.desc: Sean Fletcher is in Liverpool to meet celebrated screenwriter and author Frank Cottrell-Boyce, who chooses his favourite hymns and reflects on life, faith and the value of wonder.

programme.title: Nativity 2: Danger in the Manger!
programme.desc: An anxious teacher starts a new job at an under-achieving school and quickly finds himself struggling to cope with a wild classroom assistant, a group of under-performing kids and his own very pregnant wife. He soon becomes embroiled in a madcap plan to enter a national Song for Christmas competition and finds himself embarking on a disastrous road trip in search of the competition venue - the Christmas Castle. Lost in the wilderness with a class of small children, a baby and a donkey, he has to stand up, face his fears and try to lead them not only to safety, but victory.

programme.title: Blue Planet III
programme.desc: From winter storms to scorching summers, seasonal seas push animals to be resourceful, adaptable and adventurous. Those who can survive these dynamic seas reap rich rewards.

programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.desc: The latest news, sport and weather for the North East and Cumbria.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Charlotte Smith and Sean Fletcher are in the Ceiriog Valley in north Wales, meeting former clinical vet Claire Whittle, who took on an upland farm two years ago. Charlotte finds out why Claire made the leap into farming and what regenerative farming means to her, before helping with health and pregnancy checks on her cattle. Sean gets stuck into a cow pat to explore the hidden world of dung beetles and helps plant trees in a new agroforestry field. Meanwhile, Tom investigates changes that could be coming for the game bird shooting industry.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: The roadshow comes from Alexandra Gardens in the heart of Cardiff, where treasures include a Maori pipe, a book listing wartime spies and a rare SAS medal collection. Ronnie Archer-Morgan is thrilled to see a pipe by a renowned Maori craftsman, whilst Geoffrey Munn is dazzled by a jewel-encrusted stick pin given as a gift from King Edward VII and Queen Alexandra. There are plenty of Welsh treasures to be found, including an autograph book featuring a Tom Jones signature and early concert ticket, and Lisa Lloyd challenges Fiona to spot the most valuable item in a group of three pieces of rare rugby memorabilia. Marc Allum is stunned to see a remarkable archive of First World War-era photographs documenting arrivals into Cardiff Docks, some of whom were suspected of being spies, and militaria expert Mark Smith is humbled by a group of medals and a cap badge belonging to one of the earliest members of the SAS. Fiona Bruce finds out about the long history of Alexandra Gardens as a war memorial when she meets Simon Weston, veteran of the Falklands conflict.

programme.title: Strictly Come Dancing
programme.desc: It’s part two of the Blackpool spectacular, and we’re back in the Tower Ballroom for the results. The pros hit the dance floor for another dazzling group performance before two couples must dance again to try to keep their place in the competition. Who will dance for the final time in Blackpool? And who will return for an Instant Dance next weekend?

programme.title: Blue Planet III
programme.desc: A look at the surprising connections between the world's oceans, from the icy worlds of the poles to unexpected coasts closer to home.

programme.title: The Witch Farm
programme.desc: Summer 1989. Looking for a fresh start, Bill and his pregnant partner Liz move to a remote farmhouse in the idyllic Brecon Beacons with his teenage son Jonathan. Yet on the very first night, Liz hears footsteps on the landing. Before long, she and Jonathan are sharing disturbing dreams. And as strange events intensify, Bill and Liz are forced to accept a terrifying new reality.

In a Brackley antiques centre, two teams hope to find some blockbuster buys of their own, helped by leading men Tim Weeks and Thomas Forrester. programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Charlotte Smith and Sean Fletcher are in the Ceiriog Valley in north Wales, meeting former clinical vet Claire Whittle, who took on an upland farm two years ago. Charlotte finds out why Claire made the leap into farming and what regenerative farming means to her, before helping with health and pregnancy checks on her cattle. Sean gets stuck into a cow pat to explore the hidden world of dung beetles and helps plant trees in a new agroforestry field. Meanwhile, Tom investigates changes that could be coming for the game bird shooting industry.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: The roadshow comes from Alexandra Gardens in the heart of Cardiff, where treasures include a Maori pipe, a book listing wartime spies and a rare SAS medal collection. Ronnie Archer-Morgan is thrilled to see a pipe by a renowned Maori craftsman, whilst Geoffrey Munn is dazzled by a jewel-encrusted stick pin given as a gift from King Edward VII and Queen Alexandra. There are plenty of Welsh treasures to be found, including an autograph book featuring a Tom Jones signature and early concert ticket, and Lisa Lloyd challenges Fiona to spot the most valuable item in a group of three pieces of rare rugby memorabilia. Marc Allum is stunned to see a remarkable archive of First World War-era photographs documenting arrivals into Cardiff Docks, some of whom were suspected of being spies, and militaria expert Mark Smith is humbled by a group of medals and a cap badge belonging to one of the earliest members of the SAS. Fiona Bruce finds out about the long history of Alexandra Gardens as a war memorial when she meets Simon Weston, veteran of the Falklands conflict.

programme.title: Strictly Come Dancing
programme.desc: It’s part two of the Blackpool spectacular, and we’re back in the Tower Ballroom for the results. The pros hit the dance floor for another dazzling group performance before two couples must dance again to try to keep their place in the competition. Who will dance for the final time in Blackpool? And who will return for an Instant Dance next weekend?

programme.title: Blue Planet III
programme.desc: A look at the surprising connections between the world's oceans, from the icy worlds of the poles to unexpected coasts closer to home.

programme.title: The Witch Farm
programme.desc: Summer 1989. Looking for a fresh start, Bill and his pregnant partner Liz move to a remote farmhouse in the idyllic Brecon Beacons with his teenage son Jonathan. Yet on the very first night, Liz hears footsteps on the landing. Before long, she and Jonathan are sharing disturbing dreams. And as strange events intensify, Bill and Liz are forced to accept a terrifying new reality.

programme.title: Dashcam Justice
programme.desc: A recovery truck ploughs into an SUV carrying a mother and daughter, sending it flying into another car. The driver insists he's done nothing wrong, but a bus dashcam holds crucial evidence. A minor moped collision sparks a claim for tens of thousands of pounds, and a fraud investigator uncovers suspicious connections. Could the claimant's own footage expose the scam? An HGV leaves a cyclist perilously short of room.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Martin, Dion and Martel check out auction property buys in Plymouth, Silsden in West Yorkshire and the village of Mytholmroyd near Hebden Bridge. The developers do a lot of the work themselves in the hope they can make a profit on their bricks-and-mortar investments.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: The teams are shopping in the mid-Wales town of Builth Wells, and Danny learns about a unique family business which immortalises rugby players and other Welsh icons in clay.

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: Denise van Outen is stepping into the fight against fraud - and this time, it’s personal. After scammers stole thousands from her in a devious bank scam two years ago, Denise is teaming up with Scam Interceptors to turn the tables. In this special episode, airing as part of BBC Scam Safe week, Denise joins Rav Wilding and the team to expose the global web of criminals targeting UK victims, including those taking advantage of her identity. Using the same remote access tech scammers rely on, the team hacks the hackers to monitor their operations in real time, before confronting them. Denise also uses voice-changing technology to have fun at the scammers’ expense.

programme.title: Doorbell Detectives
programme.desc: When one of Nottingham’s oldest businesses is broken into, staff member Becca turns Miss Marple and manages to crack the case. Former police inspector Anton Sullivan shows two residents of the doorbell detective neighbourhood the elaborate lengths thieves will go to, to get their hands on your stuff. And Matt also hears from two friends whose life savings disappeared overnight when their food truck was stolen.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Nicki Chapman is in glorious Gloucestershire with Sam and Mandy, who are moving from a harbour town in Devon and making a fresh start in the countryside, with their two much-loved dogs coming along for the adventure. With £475,000 to spend, Nicki serves up a terrific selection of homes, but it’s the mystery house that really raises the stakes, with views so spectacular they feel like they’re standing on top of the world. From one grand outlook to another, Nicki gets an exclusive invitation to experience horticulture on a truly regal scale when she visits a garden quite literally fit for a king.

programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road
programme.desc: The team help commemorate the victims of the Lockerbie bombing, automata expert Michael tackles a clockwork train, and Kirsten gets hands-on with medieval slipware pottery.

programme.title: The Finish Line
programme.desc: Roman Kemp, assisted by Sarah Greene, hosts the quiz show where contestants race in moving podiums across the studio floor. Five contestants - Amanda, Jamie, Iain, Namita and Chris - battle across a series of fast-paced qualifiers and head-to-head races where the aim of the game is simple – make it to the finish line before your rivals. The winner then races against the track itself in an attempt to win the £5,000 cash prize.

programme.desc: Alexander Armstrong is joined by co-host Vick Hope for the brainy quiz where the contestants try to score as few points as possible by plumbing the depths of their general knowledge to come up with the answers no-one else could think of.

Bethan offers to conduct a seance, leading to a shocking conclusion.

programme.desc: The doors of Slane Castle have opened once again, with 23 new players entering The Traitors Ireland for its second season. Hosted once again by Siobhán McSweeney, the players attempt to navigate a game built on trust, strategy and deception, forming alliances while trying to work out who among them they can believe.

programme.desc: Paul reveals his troubled past to Bridget, who encourages him to settle an old score. Matron involves Bunny in a novel cure for her insomnia as Grinner stokes fears about Wesley.

programme.title: Saturday Kitchen
programme.desc: Matt Tebbutt is joined by chefs Saliha Mahmood-Ahmed and The Beefy Boys, and by special guest Greg Wise. Drinks expert Helen McGinn picks the wines to go with the studio dishes, and there are some great moments from the BBC food archive.

programme.title: Simply Nigella
programme.desc: There is another serving of irresistibly easy dishes on offer as Nigella rustles up more of her favourite recipes that promise to help with the wind down at the end of a long day. This time, the focus is on ensuring a cosy and comforting vibe. Breakfast is a tray of cheering chai muffins - light, luscious and dairy-free. For a low-key lunch, there are Nigella's Asian-flavoured short ribs - a perfect make-ahead, meltingly tender beef stew. And friends are in for an informal supper with Nigella's fish tacos. Inspired by her visits to Tacoria's on America's west coast, Nigella's homemade, oven-baked version involves a bit of DIY at the table, ensuring a laid-back atmosphere for guests and host alike. The tacos are followed by a divine salted chocolate tart for pudding.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: This special show is just what the doctor ordered! Experts Gary Pe and Steph Connell help actors Dex Lee, Kia Pegg, Sarah Moyle and Dido Miles in their hunt for healthy profits.

programme.title: The Football Interview
programme.desc: The Football Interview sees the biggest names in sport and entertainment join host Kelly Somers for bold, in-depth conversations about the nation’s favourite sport. We explore mindset and motivation, reflect on defining moments and career highs, and discuss personal insights. It’s a chance to show an honest, human and sometimes surprising side to familiar faces. At the heart of this is Kelly Somers – one of the most trusted, versatile and authentic voices in sports broadcasting. Kelly brings a brand of warmth and relatability that resonates with both athletes and audiences. What sets her apart is her ability to dig deeper with a sensitive approach, creating a space where athletes feel comfortable being open, honest and at times vulnerable. Each episode sees Kelly draw out stories and insight from the player behind the name about the beautiful game, their origins and values, and a look-ahead to the future from a sporting and personal perspective. She takes her subjects on a journey – and takes the viewer with her.

Charlotte finds out why Claire made the leap into farming and what regenerative farming means to her, before helping with health and pregnancy checks on her cattle. Sean gets stuck into a cow pat to explore the hidden world of dung beetles and helps plant trees in a new agroforestry field. Meanwhile, Tom investigates changes that could be coming for the game bird shooting industry.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: The roadshow comes from Alexandra Gardens in the heart of Cardiff, where treasures include a Maori pipe, a book listing wartime spies and a rare SAS medal collection. Ronnie Archer-Morgan is thrilled to see a pipe by a renowned Maori craftsman, whilst Geoffrey Munn is dazzled by a jewel-encrusted stick pin given as a gift from King Edward VII and Queen Alexandra. There are plenty of Welsh treasures to be found, including an autograph book featuring a Tom Jones signature and early concert ticket, and Lisa Lloyd challenges Fiona to spot the most valuable item in a group of three pieces of rare rugby memorabilia. Marc Allum is stunned to see a remarkable archive of First World War-era photographs documenting arrivals into Cardiff Docks, some of whom were suspected of being spies, and militaria expert Mark Smith is humbled by a group of medals and a cap badge belonging to one of the earliest members of the SAS. Fiona Bruce finds out about the long history of Alexandra Gardens as a war memorial when she meets Simon Weston, veteran of the Falklands conflict.

programme.title: Strictly Come Dancing
programme.desc: It’s part two of the Blackpool spectacular, and we’re back in the Tower Ballroom for the results. The pros hit the dance floor for another dazzling group performance before two couples must dance again to try to keep their place in the competition. Who will dance for the final time in Blackpool? And who will return for an Instant Dance next weekend?

programme.title: Blue Planet III
programme.desc: A look at the surprising connections between the world's oceans, from the icy worlds of the poles to unexpected coasts closer to home.

programme.title: The Witch Farm
programme.desc: Summer 1989. Looking for a fresh start, Bill and his pregnant partner Liz move to a remote farmhouse in the idyllic Brecon Beacons with his teenage son Jonathan. Yet on the very first night, Liz hears footsteps on the landing. Before long, she and Jonathan are sharing disturbing dreams. And as strange events intensify, Bill and Liz are forced to accept a terrifying new reality.

programme.title: Dashcam Justice
programme.desc: A recovery truck ploughs into an SUV carrying a mother and daughter, sending it flying into another car. The driver insists he's done nothing wrong, but a bus dashcam holds crucial evidence. A minor moped collision sparks a claim for tens of thousands of pounds, and a fraud investigator uncovers suspicious connections. Could the claimant's own footage expose the scam? An HGV leaves a cyclist perilously short of room.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Martin, Dion and Martel check out auction property buys in Plymouth, Silsden in West Yorkshire and the village of Mytholmroyd near Hebden Bridge. The developers do a lot of the work themselves in the hope they can make a profit on their bricks-and-mortar investments.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: The teams are shopping in the mid-Wales town of Builth Wells, and Danny learns about a unique family business which immortalises rugby players and other Welsh icons in clay.

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: Denise van Outen is stepping into the fight against fraud - and this time, it’s personal. After scammers stole thousands from her in a devious bank scam two years ago, Denise is teaming up with Scam Interceptors to turn the tables. In this special episode, airing as part of BBC Scam Safe week, Denise joins Rav Wilding and the team to expose the global web of criminals targeting UK victims, including those taking advantage of her identity. Using the same remote access tech scammers rely on, the team hacks the hackers to monitor their operations in real time, before confronting them. Denise also uses voice-changing technology to have fun at the scammers’ expense.

programme.title: Doorbell Detectives
programme.desc: When one of Nottingham’s oldest businesses is broken into, staff member Becca turns Miss Marple and manages to crack the case. Former police inspector Anton Sullivan shows two residents of the doorbell detective neighbourhood the elaborate lengths thieves will go to, to get their hands on your stuff. And Matt also hears from two friends whose life savings disappeared overnight when their food truck was stolen.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Nicki Chapman is in glorious Gloucestershire with Sam and Mandy, who are moving from a harbour town in Devon and making a fresh start in the countryside, with their two much-loved dogs coming along for the adventure. With £475,000 to spend, Nicki serves up a terrific selection of homes, but it’s the mystery house that really raises the stakes, with views so spectacular they feel like they’re standing on top of the world. From one grand outlook to another, Nicki gets an exclusive invitation to experience horticulture on a truly regal scale when she visits a garden quite literally fit for a king.

programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road
programme.desc: The team help commemorate the victims of the Lockerbie bombing, automata expert Michael tackles a clockwork train, and Kirsten gets hands-on with medieval slipware pottery.

programme.title: The Finish Line
programme.desc: Roman Kemp, assisted by Sarah Greene, hosts the quiz show where contestants race in moving podiums across the studio floor. Correct answers get the players moving, while wrong answers will stop them in their tracks. Five contestants - Amanda, Jamie, Iain, Namita and Chris - battle across a series of fast-paced qualifiers and head-to-head races where the aim of the game is simple – make it to the finish line before your rivals. The winner then races against the track itself in an attempt to win the £5,000 cash prize.

programme.title: Pointless
programme.desc: Alexander Armstrong is joined by co-host Vick Hope for the brainy quiz where the contestants try to score as few points as possible by plumbing the depths of their general knowledge to come up with the answers no-one else could think of.

programme.title: The Marvellous Miniature Workshop
programme.desc: Sara Cox and the team meet Steven, a fourth-generation baker who longs to see his family’s beloved bakery brought back to life in miniature. Once the heart of local life, the business has since been lost to changing times. Can Lee Robinson capture the shopfront, the loaves and the legacy that meant everything to Steven’s family?

programme.title: The Witch Farm
programme.desc: The family receive a shockingly high electricity bill, and their animals start to behave oddly. Liz meets spiritualist Bethan at a mother and baby group. After a strained Christmas dinner, Jonathan admits he’s also seen a ghost. Liz and Bill beg Brecon Council for help, raising the suspicions of social services. Bethan offers to conduct a seance, leading to a shocking conclusion.

programme.title: BBC News at Ten
programme.desc: The latest national and international news, with reports from BBC correspondents worldwide.

programme.title: BBC Newsline
programme.desc: Local news from across Northern Ireland with Tara Mills and Declan Harvey.

programme.title: Tall Tales & Murder
programme.desc: Bee Man catches up with Paul as Bridget realises the cost of her hasty revenge. Matron’s plan to swap Grinner for Maurice goes awry when Grinner escapes and Wesley closes in.

programme.title: The Traitors Ireland
programme.desc: The doors of Slane Castle have opened once again, with 23 new players entering The Traitors Ireland for its second season. The line-up features contestants from across the country, ranging in age from 24 to 61 and including teachers, a postal worker, a psychotherapist, a musician, a stay-at-home dad, an Irish Defence Forces member, and an actor and drama teacher. Hosted once again by Siobhán McSweeney, the players attempt to navigate a game built on trust, strategy and deception, forming alliances while trying to work out who among them they can believe.

programme.title: Fall
programme.desc: A fast drop and a sudden stop await Becky (Grace Fulton) and Hunter (Virginia Gardner) as they find themselves trapped 2,000 feet up an abandoned radio tower in the desert. Highly trained and resourceful, these climbers marking the tragic passing of a friend were not ready for every eventuality. A series of unfortunate events see their gear and supplies taken from them, and as temperatures rise and vultures begin to circle, the chance of survival begins to fall rapidly. A heart-pounding tale of survival from the producers of 47 Meters Down, where sacrifice may just be the only way out.

programme.title: Saturday Kitchen
programme.desc: Matt Tebbutt is joined by chefs Saliha Mahmood-Ahmed and The Beefy Boys, and by special guest Greg Wise. Drinks expert Helen McGinn picks the wines to go with the studio dishes, and there are some great moments from the BBC food archive.

programme.title: Simply Nigella
programme.desc: There is another serving of irresistibly easy dishes on offer as Nigella rustles up more of her favourite recipes that promise to help with the wind down at the end of a long day. This time, the focus is on ensuring a cosy and comforting vibe. Breakfast is a tray of cheering chai muffins - light, luscious and dairy-free. For a low-key lunch, there are Nigella's Asian-flavoured short ribs - a perfect make-ahead, meltingly tender beef stew. And friends are in for an informal supper with Nigella's fish tacos. Inspired by her visits to Tacoria's on America's west coast, Nigella's homemade, oven-baked version involves a bit of DIY at the table, ensuring a laid-back atmosphere for guests and host alike. The tacos are followed by a divine salted chocolate tart for pudding.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: This special show is just what the doctor ordered! Experts Gary Pe and Steph Connell help actors Dex Lee, Kia Pegg, Sarah Moyle and Dido Miles in their hunt for healthy profits.

programme.title: The Football Interview
programme.desc: The Football Interview sees the biggest names in sport and entertainment join host Kelly Somers for bold, in-depth conversations about the nation’s favourite sport. We explore mindset and motivation, reflect on defining moments and career highs, and discuss personal insights. It’s a chance to show an honest, human and sometimes surprising side to familiar faces. At the heart of this is Kelly Somers – one of the most trusted, versatile and authentic voices in sports broadcasting. Kelly brings a brand of warmth and relatability that resonates with both athletes and audiences. What sets her apart is her ability to dig deeper with a sensitive approach, creating a space where athletes feel comfortable being open, honest and at times vulnerable. Each episode sees Kelly draw out stories and insight from the player behind the name about the beautiful game, their origins and values, and a look-ahead to the future from a sporting and personal perspective. She takes her subjects on a journey – and takes the viewer with her.

programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Money for Nothing
programme.desc: In Surrey, Sarah Moore is at Witley recycling centre, trawling the car boots in the hope of finding some potential gems in need of creative magic. Upcycling sisters Katie Stone and Sophie Lawrence are tested by a wooden cabinet in disrepair, four chairs in a mix of styles get a radical revamp from woodworker Martin Hough, whilst Sarah must think out of the box when she takes on a metal trunk full of vintage tools.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: A creative couple from London want to leave city life behind in search of new adventures in Gloucestershire, and Chris Bavin is on hand to guide them. Along with presenting a lovely selection of houses, Chris also visits a local football club to check out for himself why it’s green by name and green by nature.

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: The cryptocurrency scammers based in Albania are back at it as the team listen in. This group claim to help their victims recover lost investments, but in reality, they are just looking to steal more money. With efforts to get through on the phone failing, the ground team are dispatched to try to prevent a woman from Woking paying out, but local roadworks throw a spanner into the plan. As the scam nears its conclusion, Nick and Harleen watch on helplessly as ground interceptors Meea and Harriet do their utmost to beat the traffic and reach the woman in time. The team also join forces with ethical hacker Dan to investigate and confront a man from Cameroon claiming to sell horses on social media.

programme.title: BBC Children in Need
programme.desc: Five days. Four nations. 400 miles. Owain Wyn Evans takes on an epic cycling challenge across the United Kingdom, pushing himself to the limit to raise money for BBC Children in Need.

programme.desc: Jason Mohammad and guests bring you all the goals, latest drama, analysis, reaction and interviews.

programme.desc: Roman Kemp hosts this quiz show with sidekick Sarah Greene. Five celebrities, Maisie Adam, JJ Chalmers, Harry Clark, Abby Cook and Colin Jackson, race in moving podiums across a star-spangled themed studio to try to win £10,000 for their chosen charity.

programme.title: Strictly Come Dancing
programme.desc: It’s that time of year again – Strictly returns to the home of ballroom dancing, the iconic Blackpool Tower, for a spectacular night of dancing. The show begins with a group performance from the entire cast and the legendary Basement Jaxx. Then, Emma, Josh and Jojo welcome our couples to the world-famous ballroom for their biggest performances of the competition. Shirley Ballas, Craig Revel Horwood, Motsi Mabuse and Anton Du Beke have packed their paddles and will be sharing expert advice before the vote opens and you have your say. Which couple’s performance will be the talk of the tower?

programme.title: Michael McIntyre's The Wheel
programme.desc: Michael McIntyre hosts his hit game show packed with huge stars, big laughs and a giant spinning wheel. Can the contestants answer their way to a fortune? The celebrity experts in this episode are Italian Bach, Kerry Godliman, Trevor Nelson, Angela Scanlon, Alex Scott, Josh Widdicombe, Bez and Shaun Ryder.

programme.title: Honey
programme.desc: Martha is annoyed after Kurt steals their joint credit for locating Kamilla, and she vows to gain access to the scientist alone. A competitive Kurt promises to do the same. Friedrich is ordered by his boss Schimmel to ramp up his efforts to locate Greta, believing she is the key to the Hermann Metzl case. Eager for a win, Martha and Kurt attempt to insinuate their way into Friedrich’s confidence to find Greta. Stung by his reaction, Martha steals a prized possession.
