programme.title: The Sunday Show
programme.desc: Gary Robertson brings you all the main issues from the world of politics and beyond. Big interviews, discussion and analysis of the stories that matter to Scotland.

programme.title: Sunday Morning Live
programme.desc: Sean Fletcher and Holly Hamilton host a pre-recorded, end-of-year episode of the show that puts the heart and soul into Sundays, bringing faith and ethics to the discussions that matter most. We reflect on a year when warnings of the risks facing humanity have regularly been in the news and examine the impact these themes could have on society as we ask: can a crisis bring us together? And, a year after Dame Sarah Mullally was formally elected as archbishop of Canterbury, we discuss what the future of the church could look like. We also hear the story of the Scottish teenager who could become a saint.

programme.title: Celebration Kitchen
programme.desc: Matt Tebbutt is joined by chefs Gurdeep Loyal, Ravinder Bhogal and Manpreet Singh. Celebrity guests Ranvir Singh, Dr Ranj and Sathnam Sanghera celebrate the Sikh festival Guru Nanak Gurpurab.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: From the Golden Globes to the Emmys, it’s awards season on the show as Natasha Raskin Sharp marvels at movie memorabilia, all owned by a familiar face – Bargain Hunt expert and film fan Stephanie Connell. Steph shares with Natasha items from her own collection, including awards given to Sir John Gielgud and an original prop from 1970 film Julius Caesar, starring Charlton Heston. In a Brackley antiques centre, two teams hope to find some blockbuster buys of their own, helped by leading men Tim Weeks and Thomas Forrester. And in the grand finale at the auction in Derbyshire, auctioneer James Lewis gives his verdict on the teams’ items.

programme.title: Simply Nigella
programme.desc: There is another serving of irresistibly easy dishes on offer as Nigella rustles up more of her favourite recipes that promise to help with the wind down at the end of a long day. This time, the focus is on ensuring a cosy and comforting vibe. Breakfast is a tray of cheering chai muffins - light, luscious and dairy-free. For a low-key lunch, there are Nigella's Asian-flavoured short ribs - a perfect make-ahead, meltingly tender beef stew. And friends are in for an informal supper with Nigella's fish tacos. Inspired by her visits to Tacoria's on America's west coast, Nigella's homemade, oven-baked version involves a bit of DIY at the table, ensuring a laid-back atmosphere for guests and host alike. The tacos are followed by a divine salted chocolate tart for pudding.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt

programme.title: The Football Interview
programme.desc: The Football Interview sees the biggest names in sport and entertainment join host Kelly Somers for bold, in-depth conversations about the nation’s favourite sport. We explore mindset and motivation, reflect on defining moments and career highs, and discuss personal insights. It’s a chance to show an honest, human and sometimes surprising side to familiar faces. At the heart of this is Kelly Somers – one of the most trusted, versatile and authentic voices in sports broadcasting. Kelly brings a brand of warmth and relatability that resonates with both athletes and audiences. What sets her apart is her ability to dig deeper with a sensitive approach, creating a space where athletes feel comfortable being open, honest and at times vulnerable. Each episode sees Kelly draw out stories and insight from the player behind the name about the beautiful game, their origins and values, and a look-ahead to the future from a sporting and personal perspective. She takes her subjects on a journey – and takes the viewer with her.

programme.title: Strictly Come Dancing

programme.title: Honey
programme.desc: Martha is annoyed after Kurt steals their joint credit for locating Kamilla, and she vows to gain access to the scientist alone. A competitive Kurt promises to do the same. Friedrich is ordered by his boss Schimmel to ramp up his efforts to locate Greta, believing she is the key to the Hermann Metzl case. Eager for a win, Martha and Kurt attempt to insinuate their way into Friedrich’s confidence to find Greta. Stung by his reaction, Martha steals a prized possession.

Adapted by David Nicholls for BBC Films from the novel by Thomas Hardy.

programme.title: Sunday Morning Live
programme.desc: Sean Fletcher and Holly Hamilton host a pre-recorded, end-of-year episode of the show that puts the heart and soul into Sundays, bringing faith and ethics to the discussions that matter most. We reflect on a year when warnings of the risks facing humanity have regularly been in the news and examine the impact these themes could have on society as we ask: can a crisis bring us together? And, a year after Dame Sarah Mullally was formally elected as archbishop of Canterbury, we discuss what the future of the church could look like. We also hear the story of the Scottish teenager who could become a saint.

programme.title: Celebration Kitchen

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: From the Golden Globes to the Emmys, it’s awards season on the show as Natasha Raskin Sharp marvels at movie memorabilia, all owned by a familiar face – Bargain Hunt expert and film fan Stephanie Connell. Steph shares with Natasha items from her own collection, including awards given to Sir John Gielgud and an original prop from 1970 film Julius Caesar, starring Charlton Heston. In a Brackley antiques centre, two teams hope to find some blockbuster buys of their own, helped by leading men Tim Weeks and Thomas Forrester. And in the grand finale at the auction in Derbyshire, auctioneer James Lewis gives his verdict on the teams’ items.

programme.title: Nativity 2: Danger in the Manger!
programme.desc: An anxious teacher starts a new job at an under-achieving school and quickly finds himself struggling to cope with a wild classroom assistant, a group of under-performing kids and his own very pregnant wife. He soon becomes embroiled in a madcap plan to enter a national Song for Christmas competition and finds himself embarking on a disastrous road trip in search of the competition venue - the Christmas Castle. Lost in the wilderness with a class of small children, a baby and a donkey, he has to stand up, face his fears and try to lead them not only to safety, but victory.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Charlotte Smith and Sean Fletcher are in the Ceiriog Valley in north Wales, meeting former clinical vet Claire Whittle, who took on an upland farm two years ago. Charlotte finds out why Claire made the leap into farming and what regenerative farming means to her, before helping with health and pregnancy checks on her cattle. Sean gets stuck into a cow pat to explore the hidden world of dung beetles and helps plant trees in a new agroforestry field. Meanwhile, Tom investigates changes that could be coming for the game bird shooting industry.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: The roadshow comes from Alexandra Gardens in the heart of Cardiff, where treasures include a Maori pipe, a book listing wartime spies and a rare SAS medal collection. Ronnie Archer-Morgan is thrilled to see a pipe by a renowned Maori craftsman, whilst Geoffrey Munn is dazzled by a jewel-encrusted stick pin given as a gift from King Edward VII and Queen Alexandra. There are plenty of Welsh treasures to be found, including an autograph book featuring a Tom Jones signature and early concert ticket, and Lisa Lloyd challenges Fiona to spot the most valuable item in a group of three pieces of rare rugby memorabilia. Marc Allum is stunned to see a remarkable archive of First World War-era photographs documenting arrivals into Cardiff Docks, some of whom were suspected of being spies, and militaria expert Mark Smith is humbled by a group of medals and a cap badge belonging to one of the earliest members of the SAS. Fiona Bruce finds out about the long history of Alexandra Gardens as a war memorial when she meets Simon Weston, veteran of the Falklands conflict.

programme.title: Strictly Come Dancing
programme.desc: It’s part two of the Blackpool spectacular, and we’re back in the Tower Ballroom for the results. The pros hit the dance floor for another dazzling group performance before two couples must dance again to try to keep their place in the competition. Who will dance for the final time in Blackpool? And who will return for an Instant Dance next weekend?

programme.title: The Witch Farm
programme.desc: Summer 1989. Looking for a fresh start, Bill and his pregnant partner Liz move to a remote farmhouse in the idyllic Brecon Beacons with his teenage son Jonathan. Yet on the very first night, Liz hears footsteps on the landing. Before long, she and Jonathan are sharing disturbing dreams. And as strange events intensify, Bill and Liz are forced to accept a terrifying new reality.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Charlotte Smith and Sean Fletcher are in the Ceiriog Valley in north Wales, meeting former clinical vet Claire Whittle, who took on an upland farm two years ago. Charlotte finds out why Claire made the leap into farming and what regenerative farming means to her, before helping with health and pregnancy checks on her cattle. Sean gets stuck into a cow pat to explore the hidden world of dung beetles and helps plant trees in a new agroforestry field. Meanwhile, Tom investigates changes that could be coming for the game bird shooting industry.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: The roadshow comes from Alexandra Gardens in the heart of Cardiff, where treasures include a Maori pipe, a book listing wartime spies and a rare SAS medal collection. Ronnie Archer-Morgan is thrilled to see a pipe by a renowned Maori craftsman, whilst Geoffrey Munn is dazzled by a jewel-encrusted stick pin given as a gift from King Edward VII and Queen Alexandra. There are plenty of Welsh treasures to be found, including an autograph book featuring a Tom Jones signature and early concert ticket, and Lisa Lloyd challenges Fiona to spot the most valuable item in a group of three pieces of rare rugby memorabilia. Marc Allum is stunned to see a remarkable archive of First World War-era photographs documenting arrivals into Cardiff Docks, some of whom were suspected of being spies, and militaria expert Mark Smith is humbled by a group of medals and a cap badge belonging to one of the earliest members of the SAS. Fiona Bruce finds out about the long history of Alexandra Gardens as a war memorial when she meets Simon Weston, veteran of the Falklands conflict.

programme.title: Strictly Come Dancing
programme.desc: It’s part two of the Blackpool spectacular, and we’re back in the Tower Ballroom for the results. And who will return for an Instant Dance next weekend?

programme.title: The Witch Farm

And as strange events intensify, Bill and Liz are forced to accept a terrifying new reality.

programme.desc: A recovery truck ploughs into an SUV carrying a mother and daughter, sending it flying into another car. A minor moped collision sparks a claim for tens of thousands of pounds, and a fraud investigator uncovers suspicious connections. Could the claimant's own footage expose the scam? An HGV leaves a cyclist perilously short of room.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Martin, Dion and Martel check out auction property buys in Plymouth, Silsden in West Yorkshire and the village of Mytholmroyd near Hebden Bridge. The developers do a lot of the work themselves in the hope they can make a profit on their bricks-and-mortar investments.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: The teams are shopping in the mid-Wales town of Builth Wells, and Danny learns about a unique family business which immortalises rugby players and other Welsh icons in clay.

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: Denise van Outen is stepping into the fight against fraud - and this time, it’s personal. After scammers stole thousands from her in a devious bank scam two years ago, Denise is teaming up with Scam Interceptors to turn the tables. In this special episode, airing as part of BBC Scam Safe week, Denise joins Rav Wilding and the team to expose the global web of criminals targeting UK victims, including those taking advantage of her identity. Using the same remote access tech scammers rely on, the team hacks the hackers to monitor their operations in real time, before confronting them. Denise also uses voice-changing technology to have fun at the scammers’ expense.

programme.title: Doorbell Detectives
programme.desc: When one of Nottingham’s oldest businesses is broken into, staff member Becca turns Miss Marple and manages to crack the case. Former police inspector Anton Sullivan shows two residents of the doorbell detective neighbourhood the elaborate lengths thieves will go to, to get their hands on your stuff. And Matt also hears from two friends whose life savings disappeared overnight when their food truck was stolen.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Nicki Chapman is in glorious Gloucestershire with Sam and Mandy, who are moving from a harbour town in Devon and making a fresh start in the countryside, with their two much-loved dogs coming along for the adventure. With £475,000 to spend, Nicki serves up a terrific selection of homes, but it’s the mystery house that really raises the stakes, with views so spectacular they feel like they’re standing on top of the world. From one grand outlook to another, Nicki gets an exclusive invitation to experience horticulture on a truly regal scale when she visits a garden quite literally fit for a king.

programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road
programme.desc: The team help commemorate the victims of the Lockerbie bombing, automata expert Michael tackles a clockwork train, and Kirsten gets hands-on with medieval slipware pottery.

programme.title: The Finish Line
programme.desc: Roman Kemp, assisted by Sarah Greene, hosts the quiz show where contestants race in moving podiums across the studio floor. Correct answers get the players moving, while wrong answers will stop them in their tracks. Five contestants - Amanda, Jamie, Iain, Namita and Chris - battle across a series of fast-paced qualifiers and head-to-head races where the aim of the game is simple – make it to the finish line before your rivals. The winner then races against the track itself in an attempt to win the £5,000 cash prize.

programme.title: Pointless
programme.desc: Alexander Armstrong is joined by co-host Vick Hope for the brainy quiz where the contestants try to score as few points as possible by plumbing the depths of their general knowledge to come up with the answers no-one else could think of.

programme.title: The Witch Farm

Bethan offers to conduct a seance, leading to a shocking conclusion.

programme.title: The Traitors Ireland
programme.desc: The doors of Slane Castle have opened once again, with 23 new players entering The Traitors Ireland for its second season. The line-up features contestants from across the country, ranging in age from 24 to 61 and including teachers, a postal worker, a psychotherapist, a musician, a stay-at-home dad, an Irish Defence Forces member, and an actor and drama teacher. Hosted once again by Siobhán McSweeney, the players attempt to navigate a game built on trust, strategy and deception, forming alliances while trying to work out who among them they can believe.

programme.title: Saturday Kitchen
programme.desc: Matt Tebbutt is joined by chefs Saliha Mahmood-Ahmed and The Beefy Boys, and by special guest Greg Wise. Drinks expert Helen McGinn picks the wines to go with the studio dishes, and there are some great moments from the BBC food archive.

programme.title: Simply Nigella
programme.desc: There is another serving of irresistibly easy dishes on offer as Nigella rustles up more of her favourite recipes that promise to help with the wind down at the end of a long day. This time, the focus is on ensuring a cosy and comforting vibe. Breakfast is a tray of cheering chai muffins - light, luscious and dairy-free. For a low-key lunch, there are Nigella's Asian-flavoured short ribs - a perfect make-ahead, meltingly tender beef stew. And friends are in for an informal supper with Nigella's fish tacos. Inspired by her visits to Tacoria's on America's west coast, Nigella's homemade, oven-baked version involves a bit of DIY at the table, ensuring a laid-back atmosphere for guests and host alike. The tacos are followed by a divine salted chocolate tart for pudding.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: This special show is just what the doctor ordered! Experts Gary Pe and Steph Connell help actors Dex Lee, Kia Pegg, Sarah Moyle and Dido Miles in their hunt for healthy profits.

programme.title: The Football Interview
programme.desc: The Football Interview sees the biggest names in sport and entertainment join host Kelly Somers for bold, in-depth conversations about the nation’s favourite sport. We explore mindset and motivation, reflect on defining moments and career highs, and discuss personal insights. It’s a chance to show an honest, human and sometimes surprising side to familiar faces. At the heart of this is Kelly Somers – one of the most trusted, versatile and authentic voices in sports broadcasting. Kelly brings a brand of warmth and relatability that resonates with both athletes and audiences. What sets her apart is her ability to dig deeper with a sensitive approach, creating a space where athletes feel comfortable being open, honest and at times vulnerable. Each episode sees Kelly draw out stories and insight from the player behind the name about the beautiful game, their origins and values, and a look-ahead to the future from a sporting and personal perspective. She takes her subjects on a journey – and takes the viewer with her.

Upcycling sisters Katie Stone and Sophie Lawrence are tested by a wooden cabinet in disrepair, four chairs in a mix of styles get a radical revamp from woodworker Martin Hough, whilst Sarah must think out of the box when she takes on a metal trunk full of vintage tools.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Martin is overcome by the mould at a Southampton semi. Owain loves the 70s period charm on offer in Herefordshire. And Jacqui is in upmarket Chelsea, but the flat she’s in is not as fashionable as the area... at least for now!

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: A creative couple from London want to leave city life behind in search of new adventures in Gloucestershire, and Chris Bavin is on hand to guide them. programme.title: Strictly Come Dancing
programme.desc: It’s that time of year again – Strictly returns to the home of ballroom dancing, the iconic Blackpool Tower, for a spectacular night of dancing. The show begins with a group performance from the entire cast and the legendary Basement Jaxx. Then, Emma, Josh and Jojo welcome our couples to the world-famous ballroom for their biggest performances of the competition. Shirley Ballas, Craig Revel Horwood, Motsi Mabuse and Anton Du Beke have packed their paddles and will be sharing expert advice before the vote opens and you have your say. programme.title: Honey
programme.desc: Martha is annoyed after Kurt steals their joint credit for locating Kamilla, and she vows to gain access to the scientist alone. A competitive Kurt promises to do the same. Friedrich is ordered by his boss Schimmel to ramp up his efforts to locate Greta, believing she is the key to the Hermann Metzl case. Eager for a win, Martha and Kurt attempt to insinuate their way into Friedrich’s confidence to find Greta. Stung by his reaction, Martha steals a prized possession.

programme.title: Simply Nigella
programme.desc: There is another serving of irresistibly easy dishes on offer as Nigella rustles up more of her favourite recipes that promise to help with the wind down at the end of a long day. This time, the focus is on ensuring a cosy and comforting vibe. Breakfast is a tray of cheering chai muffins - light, luscious and dairy-free. For a low-key lunch, there are Nigella's Asian-flavoured short ribs - a perfect make-ahead, meltingly tender beef stew. And friends are in for an informal supper with Nigella's fish tacos. Inspired by her visits to Tacoria's on America's west coast, Nigella's homemade, oven-baked version involves a bit of DIY at the table, ensuring a laid-back atmosphere for guests and host alike. The tacos are followed by a divine salted chocolate tart for pudding.

programme.title: The Football Interview
programme.desc: The Football Interview sees the biggest names in sport and entertainment join host Kelly Somers for bold, in-depth conversations about the nation’s favourite sport. We explore mindset and motivation, reflect on defining moments and career highs, and discuss personal insights. It’s a chance to show an honest, human and sometimes surprising side to familiar faces. At the heart of this is Kelly Somers – one of the most trusted, versatile and authentic voices in sports broadcasting. Kelly brings a brand of warmth and relatability that resonates with both athletes and audiences. What sets her apart is her ability to dig deeper with a sensitive approach, creating a space where athletes feel comfortable being open, honest and at times vulnerable. Each episode sees Kelly draw out stories and insight from the player behind the name about the beautiful game, their origins and values, and a look-ahead to the future from a sporting and personal perspective. She takes her subjects on a journey – and takes the viewer with her.

Steph shares with Natasha items from her own collection, including awards given to Sir John Gielgud and an original prop from 1970 film Julius Caesar, starring Charlton Heston. In a Brackley antiques centre, two teams hope to find some blockbuster buys of their own, helped by leading men Tim Weeks and Thomas Forrester. And in the grand finale at the auction in Derbyshire, auctioneer James Lewis gives his verdict on the teams’ items.

Charlotte finds out why Claire made the leap into farming and what regenerative farming means to her, before helping with health and pregnancy checks on her cattle. Sean gets stuck into a cow pat to explore the hidden world of dung beetles and helps plant trees in a new agroforestry field. Meanwhile, Tom investigates changes that could be coming for the game bird shooting industry.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: The roadshow comes from Alexandra Gardens in the heart of Cardiff, where treasures include a Maori pipe, a book listing wartime spies and a rare SAS medal collection. Ronnie Archer-Morgan is thrilled to see a pipe by a renowned Maori craftsman, whilst Geoffrey Munn is dazzled by a jewel-encrusted stick pin given as a gift from King Edward VII and Queen Alexandra. There are plenty of Welsh treasures to be found, including an autograph book featuring a Tom Jones signature and early concert ticket, and Lisa Lloyd challenges Fiona to spot the most valuable item in a group of three pieces of rare rugby memorabilia. Marc Allum is stunned to see a remarkable archive of First World War-era photographs documenting arrivals into Cardiff Docks, some of whom were suspected of being spies, and militaria expert Mark Smith is humbled by a group of medals and a cap badge belonging to one of the earliest members of the SAS. Fiona Bruce finds out about the long history of Alexandra Gardens as a war memorial when she meets Simon Weston, veteran of the Falklands conflict.

programme.title: Strictly Come Dancing

And as strange events intensify, Bill and Liz are forced to accept a terrifying new reality.

Steph shares with Natasha items from her own collection, including awards given to Sir John Gielgud and an original prop from 1970 film Julius Caesar, starring Charlton Heston. In a Brackley antiques centre, two teams hope to find some blockbuster buys of their own, helped by leading men Tim Weeks and Thomas Forrester. programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Charlotte Smith and Sean Fletcher are in the Ceiriog Valley in north Wales, meeting former clinical vet Claire Whittle, who took on an upland farm two years ago. Charlotte finds out why Claire made the leap into farming and what regenerative farming means to her, before helping with health and pregnancy checks on her cattle. Sean gets stuck into a cow pat to explore the hidden world of dung beetles and helps plant trees in a new agroforestry field. Meanwhile, Tom investigates changes that could be coming for the game bird shooting industry.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: The roadshow comes from Alexandra Gardens in the heart of Cardiff, where treasures include a Maori pipe, a book listing wartime spies and a rare SAS medal collection. Ronnie Archer-Morgan is thrilled to see a pipe by a renowned Maori craftsman, whilst Geoffrey Munn is dazzled by a jewel-encrusted stick pin given as a gift from King Edward VII and Queen Alexandra. There are plenty of Welsh treasures to be found, including an autograph book featuring a Tom Jones signature and early concert ticket, and Lisa Lloyd challenges Fiona to spot the most valuable item in a group of three pieces of rare rugby memorabilia. Marc Allum is stunned to see a remarkable archive of First World War-era photographs documenting arrivals into Cardiff Docks, some of whom were suspected of being spies, and militaria expert Mark Smith is humbled by a group of medals and a cap badge belonging to one of the earliest members of the SAS. Fiona Bruce finds out about the long history of Alexandra Gardens as a war memorial when she meets Simon Weston, veteran of the Falklands conflict.

programme.title: Strictly Come Dancing
programme.desc: It’s part two of the Blackpool spectacular, and we’re back in the Tower Ballroom for the results. The pros hit the dance floor for another dazzling group performance before two couples must dance again to try to keep their place in the competition. Who will dance for the final time in Blackpool? And who will return for an Instant Dance next weekend?

programme.title: Blue Planet III
programme.desc: A look at the surprising connections between the world's oceans, from the icy worlds of the poles to unexpected coasts closer to home.

programme.title: The Witch Farm
programme.desc: Summer 1989. Looking for a fresh start, Bill and his pregnant partner Liz move to a remote farmhouse in the idyllic Brecon Beacons with his teenage son Jonathan. Yet on the very first night, Liz hears footsteps on the landing. Before long, she and Jonathan are sharing disturbing dreams. And as strange events intensify, Bill and Liz are forced to accept a terrifying new reality.

programme.title: Dashcam Justice
programme.desc: A recovery truck ploughs into an SUV carrying a mother and daughter, sending it flying into another car. The driver insists he's done nothing wrong, but a bus dashcam holds crucial evidence. A minor moped collision sparks a claim for tens of thousands of pounds, and a fraud investigator uncovers suspicious connections. Could the claimant's own footage expose the scam? An HGV leaves a cyclist perilously short of room.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Martin, Dion and Martel check out auction property buys in Plymouth, Silsden in West Yorkshire and the village of Mytholmroyd near Hebden Bridge. The developers do a lot of the work themselves in the hope they can make a profit on their bricks-and-mortar investments.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: The teams are shopping in the mid-Wales town of Builth Wells, and Danny learns about a unique family business which immortalises rugby players and other Welsh icons in clay.

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: Denise van Outen is stepping into the fight against fraud - and this time, it’s personal. After scammers stole thousands from her in a devious bank scam two years ago, Denise is teaming up with Scam Interceptors to turn the tables. In this special episode, airing as part of BBC Scam Safe week, Denise joins Rav Wilding and the team to expose the global web of criminals targeting UK victims, including those taking advantage of her identity. Using the same remote access tech scammers rely on, the team hacks the hackers to monitor their operations in real time, before confronting them. Denise also uses voice-changing technology to have fun at the scammers’ expense.

programme.title: Doorbell Detectives
programme.desc: When one of Nottingham’s oldest businesses is broken into, staff member Becca turns Miss Marple and manages to crack the case. Former police inspector Anton Sullivan shows two residents of the doorbell detective neighbourhood the elaborate lengths thieves will go to, to get their hands on your stuff. And Matt also hears from two friends whose life savings disappeared overnight when their food truck was stolen.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Nicki Chapman is in glorious Gloucestershire with Sam and Mandy, who are moving from a harbour town in Devon and making a fresh start in the countryside, with their two much-loved dogs coming along for the adventure. With £475,000 to spend, Nicki serves up a terrific selection of homes, but it’s the mystery house that really raises the stakes, with views so spectacular they feel like they’re standing on top of the world. From one grand outlook to another, Nicki gets an exclusive invitation to experience horticulture on a truly regal scale when she visits a garden quite literally fit for a king.

programme.title: The Repair Shop on the Road
programme.desc: The team help commemorate the victims of the Lockerbie bombing, automata expert Michael tackles a clockwork train, and Kirsten gets hands-on with medieval slipware pottery.

programme.title: The Finish Line
programme.desc: Roman Kemp, assisted by Sarah Greene, hosts the quiz show where contestants race in moving podiums across the studio floor. Correct answers get the players moving, while wrong answers will stop them in their tracks. Five contestants - Amanda, Jamie, Iain, Namita and Chris - battle across a series of fast-paced qualifiers and head-to-head races where the aim of the game is simple – make it to the finish line before your rivals. The winner then races against the track itself in an attempt to win the £5,000 cash prize.

programme.title: Pointless
programme.desc: Alexander Armstrong is joined by co-host Vick Hope for the brainy quiz where the contestants try to score as few points as possible by plumbing the depths of their general knowledge to come up with the answers no-one else could think of.

programme.title: The Witch Farm

Bethan offers to conduct a seance, leading to a shocking conclusion.

programme.title: The Traitors Ireland
programme.desc: The doors of Slane Castle have opened once again, with 23 new players entering The Traitors Ireland for its second season. The line-up features contestants from across the country, ranging in age from 24 to 61 and including teachers, a postal worker, a psychotherapist, a musician, a stay-at-home dad, an Irish Defence Forces member, and an actor and drama teacher. Hosted once again by Siobhán McSweeney, the players attempt to navigate a game built on trust, strategy and deception, forming alliances while trying to work out who among them they can believe.

programme.title: Simply Nigella
programme.desc: There is another serving of irresistibly easy dishes on offer as Nigella rustles up more of her favourite recipes that promise to help with the wind down at the end of a long day. This time, the focus is on ensuring a cosy and comforting vibe. Breakfast is a tray of cheering chai muffins - light, luscious and dairy-free. For a low-key lunch, there are Nigella's Asian-flavoured short ribs - a perfect make-ahead, meltingly tender beef stew. And friends are in for an informal supper with Nigella's fish tacos. Inspired by her visits to Tacoria's on America's west coast, Nigella's homemade, oven-baked version involves a bit of DIY at the table, ensuring a laid-back atmosphere for guests and host alike. The tacos are followed by a divine salted chocolate tart for pudding.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: This special show is just what the doctor ordered! Experts Gary Pe and Steph Connell help actors Dex Lee, Kia Pegg, Sarah Moyle and Dido Miles in their hunt for healthy profits.

programme.title: The Football Interview
programme.desc: The Football Interview sees the biggest names in sport and entertainment join host Kelly Somers for bold, in-depth conversations about the nation’s favourite sport. We explore mindset and motivation, reflect on defining moments and career highs, and discuss personal insights. It’s a chance to show an honest, human and sometimes surprising side to familiar faces. At the heart of this is Kelly Somers – one of the most trusted, versatile and authentic voices in sports broadcasting. Kelly brings a brand of warmth and relatability that resonates with both athletes and audiences. What sets her apart is her ability to dig deeper with a sensitive approach, creating a space where athletes feel comfortable being open, honest and at times vulnerable. Each episode sees Kelly draw out stories and insight from the player behind the name about the beautiful game, their origins and values, and a look-ahead to the future from a sporting and personal perspective. She takes her subjects on a journey – and takes the viewer with her.

There are plenty of Welsh treasures to be found, including an autograph book featuring a Tom Jones signature and early concert ticket, and Lisa Lloyd challenges Fiona to spot the most valuable item in a group of three pieces of rare rugby memorabilia. Marc Allum is stunned to see a remarkable archive of First World War-era photographs documenting arrivals into Cardiff Docks, some of whom were suspected of being spies, and militaria expert Mark Smith is humbled by a group of medals and a cap badge belonging to one of the earliest members of the SAS. Fiona Bruce finds out about the long history of Alexandra Gardens as a war memorial when she meets Simon Weston, veteran of the Falklands conflict.

programme.title: Strictly Come Dancing
programme.desc: It’s part two of the Blackpool spectacular, and we’re back in the Tower Ballroom for the results. The pros hit the dance floor for another dazzling group performance before two couples must dance again to try to keep their place in the competition. Who will dance for the final time in Blackpool? And who will return for an Instant Dance next weekend?

programme.title: Blue Planet III

programme.title: The Witch Farm
programme.desc: Summer 1989. Looking for a fresh start, Bill and his pregnant partner Liz move to a remote farmhouse in the idyllic Brecon Beacons with his teenage son Jonathan. Yet on the very first night, Liz hears footsteps on the landing. Before long, she and Jonathan are sharing disturbing dreams. And as strange events intensify, Bill and Liz are forced to accept a terrifying new reality.

programme.title: Dashcam Justice
programme.desc: A recovery truck ploughs into an SUV carrying a mother and daughter, sending it flying into another car. The driver insists he's done nothing wrong, but a bus dashcam holds crucial evidence. A minor moped collision sparks a claim for tens of thousands of pounds, and a fraud investigator uncovers suspicious connections. Could the claimant's own footage expose the scam? An HGV leaves a cyclist perilously short of room.

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: Denise van Outen is stepping into the fight against fraud - and this time, it’s personal. After scammers stole thousands from her in a devious bank scam two years ago, Denise is teaming up with Scam Interceptors to turn the tables. In this special episode, airing as part of BBC Scam Safe week, Denise joins Rav Wilding and the team to expose the global web of criminals targeting UK victims, including those taking advantage of her identity. Using the same remote access tech scammers rely on, the team hacks the hackers to monitor their operations in real time, before confronting them. Denise also uses voice-changing technology to have fun at the scammers’ expense.

programme.title: Doorbell Detectives

Former police inspector Anton Sullivan shows two residents of the doorbell detective neighbourhood the elaborate lengths thieves will go to, to get their hands on your stuff. And Matt also hears from two friends whose life savings disappeared overnight when their food truck was stolen.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Nicki Chapman is in glorious Gloucestershire with Sam and Mandy, who are moving from a harbour town in Devon and making a fresh start in the countryside, with their two much-loved dogs coming along for the adventure. With £475,000 to spend, Nicki serves up a terrific selection of homes, but it’s the mystery house that really raises the stakes, with views so spectacular they feel like they’re standing on top of the world. From one grand outlook to another, Nicki gets an exclusive invitation to experience horticulture on a truly regal scale when she visits a garden quite literally fit for a king.

programme.title: Make It to Munich
programme.desc: Documentary following Ethan Walker, a promising teenage footballer from Aberdeenshire who suffered life-threatening injuries in a road traffic accident just months into a football scholarship at a US university. Aided in his recovery by pioneering Scottish surgeon (and former footballer) Professor Gordon Mackay, Ethan undertakes a charity cycle ride from Glasgow to Munich for Scotland’s opening match against Germany in Euro 2024, just nine months after his accident. Entrusted by the Scottish national team to carry the match pennant on his back for the whole journey and deliver it in time for kick-off, Ethan is accompanied by Gordon, Tartan Army foot-soldier Stephen Collie and film-maker Martyn Robertson.

programme.title: Highland Cops
programme.desc: Police investigate the disappearance of a young monk from a monastery on a remote private island in Orkney. The mystery deepens when there appears to be no evidence of how he could have left the island. In Aviemore, a rock festival erupts into violence. In Inverness, officers hunt a man after a woman is attacked in a cemetery, while campers in Fort William take a wrong turn.

programme.title: Murder Case
programme.desc: When a family home in an affluent suburb of Glasgow is deliberately set on fire, detectives race to determine who attacked the young couple staying there and why.

programme.title: Songs of Modern Scotland: Celtic Connections
programme.desc: Roddy Hart curates a sold-out concert featuring performances from Biffy Clyro’s Simon Neil, Del Amitri's Justin Currie, Eddi Reader and many more, accompanied by the orchestra from the Royal Conservatoire Scotland conducted by John Logan.

programme.title: Scotland Stands Up
programme.desc: Join Stuart Mitchell for a brilliant night of stand-up comedy, featuring Jay Lafferty, Ayo Adenekan and Krystal Evans, and a special appearance from Robert Florence. Recorded live at the Church Hill Theatre in Edinburgh, the show is packed with hilarious anecdotes and sharp one-liners from some of the best comedians in Scotland right now. Edinburgh-based American Krystal Evans finds the funny in the differences and similarities in our world views and family values, while rising star Ayo Adenekan wrestles with his identity and reveals his ambitions to become a truly unique Scottish superhero. Jay Lafferty vividly describes the challenges she faces as she gets older to an audience who couldn’t agree more, and our headliner, Robert Florence, who is making a rare stand-up appearance, dons his centurion helmet to make us laugh.

programme.title: TUNE
programme.desc: From working in a bar to counting Elton John as a fan, singer-songwriter Joesef reveals how his experience of growing up in Glasgow’s east end has shaped his sound.

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: Jean Johansson is at Beechgrove, which has had a Christmas-style makeover. As part of a series helping families get ready for a fabulous Christmas, there are ideas to get your kids creating and crafting. Plus ways to make handmade presents, fabulous food and drink tips and gift suggestions, along with the usual top gardening advice from the Beechgrove team. In this episode, it’s all about the decorations. If you are about to choose a tree, just what should you be looking for? Once you’ve got one, there is expert advice on how to light and decorate it. And if you want a break from Christmas preparation, Carole Baxter will have advice on the garden jobs to be done right now.

programme.title: Grand Tours of Scotland's Rivers
programme.desc: The River Don rises in wild land, high on the moors of the Grampian mountains. Paul follows its easterly flow from the famous Cock Bridge, where he encounters the Lonach Highlanders and a clan chief with two feathers in his cap carrying relics of the Battle of Culloden. Close to Strathdon, Paul meets an artist and sculptor who creates lifelike creatures from scrap metal, and then learns how the Aberdeen Angus became a world-beating cattle breed. At Alford, he explores an unusual transport museum and hears about an eccentric and brilliant postman who invented a steam automobile. A trip in a vintage Rolls-Royce takes Paul further along the course of the river. At Kemnay, he visits the huge quarry that once provided granite for prestigious buildings across the UK. As the river nears the sea, Paul meets a woman who wove overcoats for the Red Army. He then helps a Bulgarian couple harvest honey from their black Scottish bees before reaching the mouth of the river on the North Sea coast.

programme.title: Hamza's Hidden Wild Isles
programme.desc: Wonder is everywhere – if you know where to look. From sunny beaches to rugged moors, craggy munros to city streets, Hamza Yassin reveals amazing wildlife hidden around the UK. The limited edition booklet is no longer available to order, but you can download a version from the Open University’s website.

programme.title: Highland Cops
programme.desc: On Skye, police race to a hotel where a barman has been violently assaulted. CCTV captures the shocking attack, but the suspect has fled and officers must track him down. In Inverness, police prepare to raid a house suspected of links to a Liverpool drugs gang. And on the Western Isles, officers race to a reported home invasion in a remote village, only to discover that all is not as it seems.

programme.title: This Farming Life

programme.title: Landward
programme.desc: A special episode from north Sutherland at the top of the Scottish mainland. Dougie steps out into the Flow Country, a vast expanse of blanket peat bog, where he charts the changes in its land use and its recent designation as a Unesco World Heritage site. Arlene catches up with sheep farmer Joyce Campbell to see how she has made the switch from traditional hill farming to regenerative agriculture. Arlene also visits Strath Halladale, where she meets a man who gave up city life to run the family croft 37 years ago. She finds out how he has built a thriving timber business and brought jobs to the area. And at Loch Hope, Leanna meets the biologists working to protect precious sea trout populations.

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: Jean Johansson is at Beechgrove, which has had a Christmas-style makeover. As part of a series helping families get ready for a fabulous Christmas, there are ideas to get your kids creating and crafting. Plus ways to make handmade presents, fabulous food and drink tips and gift suggestions, along with the usual top gardening advice from the Beechgrove team. In this episode, it’s all about the decorations. If you are about to choose a tree, just what should you be looking for? Once you’ve got one, there is expert advice on how to light and decorate it. And if you want a break from Christmas preparation, Carole Baxter will have advice on the garden jobs to be done right now.

programme.desc: What is a showperson? Run away with the fair and join the family firms who bring the shows to towns and villages across the country. And meet father-and-son duo Trevor and Kristan Smith as they battle wet weather and family squabbles in Airdrie.

programme.title: Lover, Liar, Predator
programme.desc: Four women, all survivors of the same dangerous man, join forces to end their nightmare and bring him to justice. Jenni, Natalie, Shannon and Robyn waive their anonymity to tell their story in chilling detail, laying bare the confusion, intricacies and frightening realities of coercive control, and revealing how they became trapped by serial predator and sex abuser Aaron Swan. Moving back and forth in time, this documentary unpicks how Swan got away with his crimes for so long, despite twice being placed on the sex offenders register. Telling their story in their own words, the women reveal how Swan’s later victims finally found a way to put him behind bars with the help of his first wife, who had been denied her own justice decades before.

programme.title: Panorama
programme.desc: Warren Arter was seen as a star detective in the Metropolitan Police, but he was also a sexual predator. He used his position running a rape and sexual offences unit to groom and sexually exploit vulnerable women whose cases he investigated. But the Met missed a string of opportunities to stop Arter and then suspended him on full pay for almost seven years before finally dismissing him for drug offences in 2023. In 2024, he was with his wife Rebekah when she died in a hotel room in Barbados in mysterious circumstances. Reporter Noel Titheradge investigates the case that has been called the Met's 'dirty secret' and tracks down new witnesses who tell him what really happened. Could Rebekah's death have been prevented? And why didn't the Met act sooner to stop the predator in its ranks?

programme.title: Blue Peter

programme.title: Deadly 60
programme.desc: Steve Backshall heads to Oman, where he abseils to a verreaux's eagle nest, tracks down wolves and swims alongside a super pod made up of over 100 dolphins.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: Monty celebrates the rewards of winter gardening - sharing ideas, inspiration and timely jobs to keep gardeners busy now, while reminding us that warmer days lie ahead. At Longmeadow, he has hellebores to plant, peas to sow and practical advice on propagating roses. Sue Kent gets to work on her allotment, where there’s always plenty to do during the colder months, including some clever composting. Jamie Butterworth takes a tour of one of Somerset’s most imaginative topiary gardens. In Belfast, a local community tells the tale of how their once neglected alleyway has become their pride and joy. Carol Klein unearths some radical new thinking on how flowers may be adapting to climate change, while Rekha Mistry travels to RHS Garden Bridgewater to see how garden varieties of tomato and mint are put to the test.

programme.title: Naturewatch
programme.desc: The team dives into some intriguing autumn mysteries: why don’t seals drown? What is the UK’s most deadly mushroom? And what extraordinary creature has the power to keep autumn leaves alive?

programme.title: My Life at Christmas with Anita Rani
programme.desc: Anita Rani pays a Christmas visit to Baroness Floella Benjamin, a pivotal figure to generations of young TV viewers. Born in Trinidad and Tobago, Floella arrived in London at the age of ten as part of the Windrush generation. Together, they retrace that journey and reflect on Dame Floella's extraordinary life shaped by faith and the festive season: from stage actor and iconic Play School presenter to businesswoman, child rights campaigner, dame and baroness, and even playing a role in King Charles III's coronation.

programme.title: Marcus Wareing's Tales from a Kitchen Garden
programme.desc: Marcus plans to bring in some ducks, but things aren’t as simple as they seem as he heads out onto the lake to create a new home for them. Heading to Devon, he discovers the perfect breed for the smallholding and picks up some top tips and tricks on how to rear them. Back on the farm, the bounty of the kitchen garden inspires a visit to a local community fridge to learn more about how it works, before a neighbour pops over to give him a lesson on what is edible and growing wild in the hedgerows and bushes that surround the smallholding. Once the new ducks arrive and are safely in their new home, he cooks up a fantastic feast inspired by a British classic, the ploughman's lunch.

programme.title: Nadiya’s Everyday Baking
programme.desc: Nadiya shows off her easy celebration bakes, which range from a glittering meringue layer cake to a slow-cooked lamb curry fit for a feast, with an American-inspired seafood extravaganza.

programme.title: The Importance of Being Earnest
programme.desc: Screen adaptation of Oscar Wilde's celebrated play in which two Victorian gentlemen both adopt a double identity under the name of Ernest and end up in trouble when they both turn up at the same country house one weekend.

programme.title: Strangers on a Train
programme.desc: Alfred Hitchcock's suspense classic about two men who plot a perfect murder. When tennis pro Guy Haines meets smooth-talking Bruno Antony in the bar of a train, he finds the stranger sympathetic with his desire to be rid of his clinging wife. The sinister Bruno then proposes that they swap murders: Bruno will murder Guy's wife, and Guy will do away with Bruno's father. From Patricia Highsmith's novel.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: The programme comes from the Platform in Morecambe, Lancashire, which in its day was the main station bringing holidaymakers to the town. Antiques experts Charles Hanson and Catherine Southon find treasures to take to auction, including a vintage Rolex watch. Paul Martin discovers the rags-to-riches story of the town's most famous son - Eric Morecambe.

programme.title: Celebrity Antiques Road Trip
programme.desc: Broadcasting legend Bob Harris and queen of motor sports Suzi Perry burn rubber across south east England in a racy 1974 Ford Escort RS 2000. But can they flip antiques for profit? Steering them in the right direction are doyens Margie Cooper and Raj Bisram, both veteran road trippers and rivals to the core. What starts out as a hunt for music and travel collectibles changes tack very early on. Bob falls for a pair of romantic champagne flutes in a love heart stand, while Suzy steps back in time when she discovers a Japanese glass fishing float. Along the way, they learn to raise their profile through the art of silhouette portraiture, with some amazing results. But at the auction, there can be only one winner. Will Bob reach the number one spot, or will Suzy be racing for the stars?

programme.title: The Eagle Has Landed
programme.desc: All-action World War II adventure. On the morning of 6 November 1943, the military authorities in Berlin receive a simple message - 'The Eagle Has Landed'. In a daring kidnap attempt, a small force of crack German paratroopers are poised to snatch Winston Churchill and return with him to Germany. If they succeed in their mission, it could alter the course of the war. Who can stop them?

programme.title: 40 Hidden Music Treasures at the BBC
programme.desc: A collection of 40 rarely seen musical moments that don't often get to escape from the BBC vaults. Featuring Roachford on The Roland Rat Show, David Bowie on Friday Night with Jonathan Ross, Mary J Blige appearing on Davina McCall's chat show and one of Gloria Estefan's several star turns on the Royal Variety Show over the years.

programme.title: 40 Hidden Music Treasures at the BBC
programme.desc: Another deep dive into the BBC’s music archives, where the musical map is pointed away from Top of the Pops on a quest to uncover 40 rarely seen performances and hidden gems. Featuring Bronski Beat’s first BBC performance of Smalltown Boy, Rihanna’s rockier version of Umbrella, Sophie Ellis-Bextor covering Pulp’s Do You Remember the First Time? and Kate Bush pairing up for a tango during Hounds of Love. These tucked-away treats and many, many more make this a journey that musical fans are certain to treasure.

programme.title: 40 Hidden Music Treasures at the BBC
programme.desc: Expect the unexpected on this journey through the BBC’s magical music archives, a Top 40 with a difference. In a Top of the Pops-free-zone, these are the surprising songs and rare performances that aren't seen every day, taken from shows that may have been forgotten - but that definitely deserve to see daylight once again. And whilst some of the musical moments may have been hidden away, the talents involved have always been prominent - ranging from Jimi Hendrix to MC Hammer, from Dusty to Tammy, and from The Beach Boys to The Pet Shop Boys.

programme.title: Celebrity Race Across the World
programme.desc: The third leg of the race sees the teams leave behind the ancient jungles of Borneo to reach the island of Sulawesi, an Indonesian wonderland that lies far from the tourist trail. But with the end of Ramadan fast approaching, the teams must negotiate the crowds heading home for Eid al-Fitr.

programme.title: Bill's Included
programme.desc: When Bill’s wife walks out on him for the gardener, he’s left lonely and broke. In the hope of turning his life around, he lets out his spare rooms to four students. Bill is thrilled to meet his new housemates: Christian, Zahra, Hettie, and James. But when Christian keeps leaving the fridge door open, Bill has to come up with a scheme to get it shut without ruining his image as a relaxed, fun landlord. Bill’s best mate, Drew, gives him the idea to deploy an anonymous suggestions box, but this backfires when the students’ requests lead to the worst night’s sleep of his life. Bill’s neighbour and secret crush, Siobhan, suggests sending over her intimidating husband, Martin, to complain on Bill’s behalf, but when this ruse is exposed, Bill fears the students will leave him, just like his wife did. He’s grateful to learn that not only do they have nowhere else to live but they forgive him, since university is all about starting over. For better or worse, his new life truly has begun.

Along the way, the programme revisits memorable Countryfile wildlife encounters, from dolphins off Anglesey to spectacular starling murmurations at Newport Wetlands.

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
